sentences.zh: 陳循，字德遵，泰和人。

translations.literal: Chen Xun, styled Dezun, was a native of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun, whose style name was Dezun, came from Taihe.

sentences.zh: 永樂十三年進士第一。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongle he ranked first among metropolitan graduates.
translations.idiomatic: In 1415 he took first place in the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 授翰林修撰。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hanlin reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a reviser in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 習朝廷典故。

translations.literal: He mastered court precedents.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the court's institutional precedents.

sentences.zh: 帝幸北京，命取秘閣書詣行在，遂留侍焉。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Beijing, he was ordered to bring secretariat books to the traveling palace and was retained in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Beijing, Chen was ordered to bring books from the Secret Repository to the traveling court and remained there in attendance.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年，進侍講。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongxi he was promoted to lecturing reader.
translations.idiomatic: In 1425 he was promoted to lecturing reader.

sentences.zh: 宣德初，受命直南宮，日承顧問。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuande he was ordered to serve in the Southern Palace and daily received imperial consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xuande reign he was assigned to the Southern Palace and received the emperor's counsel every day.

sentences.zh: 賜第玉河橋西，巡幸未嘗不從。

translations.literal: He was granted a residence west of Jade River Bridge; on imperial tours he was never absent.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted him a residence west of Jade River Bridge, and he never failed to accompany the emperor on tour.

sentences.zh: 進侍講學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to lecturing academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to lecturing academician.

sentences.zh: 正統元年兼經筵官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong he also served as classics lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: In 1436 he also served on the Classics Lecture.

sentences.zh: 久之，進翰林院學士。

translations.literal: After a long while he was promoted to Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he was promoted to Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 九年入文淵閣，典機務。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he entered the Wenyuan Pavilion and directed state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1444 he entered the Wenyuan Pavilion and took charge of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，廷議天下吏民建言章奏，皆三楊主之。

translations.literal: At first, when the court deliberated memorials and proposals from officials and commoners throughout the realm, the Three Yangs presided.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Three Yangs had handled all court deliberation on memorials from officials and commoners across the empire.

sentences.zh: 至是榮、士奇已卒，循及曹鼐、馬愉在內閣，禮部援故事請。

translations.literal: By then Rong and Shiqi had died; Xun, Cao Qi, and Ma Yu were in the Grand Secretariat, and the Ministry of Rites cited precedent in requesting.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yang Rong and Yang Shiqi had died; Chen Xun, Cao Qi, and Ma Yu sat in the Grand Secretariat, and the Ministry of Rites cited precedent in petitioning the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝以楊溥老，宜優閑，令循等預議。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering Yang Pu old and fit for ease, ordered Xun and the others to participate in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought Yang Pu too old for heavy duties and should be spared; he ordered Chen Xun and the others to join the deliberations.

sentences.zh: 明年進戶部右侍郎，兼學士。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue, retaining his academician post.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue while retaining his academician title.

sentences.zh: 土木之變，人心洶懼。

translations.literal: At the Tumu disaster popular feeling was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tumu disaster public alarm was widespread.

sentences.zh: 循居中，所言多采納。

translations.literal: Xun held the center; most of what he said was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun held a central role, and most of his counsel was adopted.

sentences.zh: 進戶部尚書，兼職如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of Revenue, his concurrent posts unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Revenue while keeping his other posts.

sentences.zh: 也先犯京師，請敕各邊精騎入衛，馳檄回番以疑敵。

translations.literal: When Esen attacked the capital, he requested imperial orders for elite cavalry from all frontiers to enter guard duty and dispatched urgent proclamations to the Western Regions to confuse the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen threatened the capital, he urged that elite cavalry from every frontier be summoned to defend the city and that urgent dispatches be sent to the Western Regions to sow doubt among the enemy.

sentences.zh: 帝皆從其計。

translations.literal: The emperor followed all his plans.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted every one of these measures.

sentences.zh: 景泰二年，以葬妻與鄉人爭墓地，為前後巡按御史所不直，循輒訐奏。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingtai, over burying his wife he disputed grave land with a fellow townsman; successive touring censors found against him, and Xun repeatedly impeached them in return.
translations.idiomatic: In 1451, while burying his wife, he quarreled with a fellow townsman over a grave site; successive touring censors ruled against him, and Chen Xun repeatedly struck back with impeachments.

sentences.zh: 給事中林聰等極論循罪。

translations.literal: The supervising secretaries Lin Cong and others argued Xun's offenses to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries including Lin Cong denounced Chen Xun's conduct in the strongest terms.

sentences.zh: 帝是聰言，而置循不問。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed with Cong's words but left Xun unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted Lin Cong's argument but took no action against Chen Xun.

sentences.zh: 循本以才望顯，及是素譽隳焉。

translations.literal: Xun had originally been eminent for talent and reputation; from this his standing was ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun had risen on talent and reputation, but this affair destroyed his standing among scholars.

sentences.zh: 二年十二月進少保兼文淵閣大學士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year he was promoted to Junior Guardian and Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of that year he was promoted to Junior Guardian and Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 帝欲易太子，內畏諸閣臣，先期賜循及高谷白金百兩，江淵、王一寧、蕭鎡半之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to change the heir apparent and inwardly feared the grand secretaries; beforehand he bestowed on Xun and Gao Gu one hundred taels of white silver each, and on Jiang Yuan, Wang Yining, and Xiao Zi half that amount.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to replace the heir apparent and feared opposition from the grand secretaries; he preemptively gave Chen Xun and Gao Gu one hundred taels of silver each and Jiang Yuan, Wang Yining, and Xiao Zi half as much.

sentences.zh: 比下詔議，循等遂不敢諍，加兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued for deliberation, Xun and the others dared not remonstrate; he was additionally made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued for deliberation, Chen Xun and the others did not dare object; he was also made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋以太子令旨賜百官銀帛。

translations.literal: Soon, by order of the heir apparent, silver and silks were bestowed on all officials.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, on the heir apparent's order, silver and silks were distributed to the entire bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 逾月，帝復賜循等六人黃金五十兩，進華蓋殿大學士，兼文淵閣如故。

translations.literal: After more than a month the emperor again bestowed fifty taels of gold on the six including Xun, promoted him to Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall, and his concurrent Wenyuan post remained.
translations.idiomatic: A month later the emperor gave Chen Xun and five colleagues fifty taels of gold each, promoted him to Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall, and left his Wenyuan post unchanged.

sentences.zh: 循子英及王文子倫應順天鄉試被黜，相與構考官劉儼、黃諫，為給事中張寧等所劾。

translations.literal: Xun's son Ying and Wang Wen's son Lun, having failed the Shuntian provincial examination, together framed the examiners Liu Yan and Huang Jian and were impeached by the supervising secretaries Zhang Ning and others.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun's son Ying and Wang Wen's son Lun failed the Shuntian provincial examination and together framed the examiners Liu Yan and Huang Jian; supervising secretaries led by Zhang Ning impeached them.

sentences.zh: 帝亦不罪。

translations.literal: The emperor also did not punish them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again declined to punish them.

sentences.zh: 英宗復位，于謙、王文死，杖循百，戍鐵嶺衛。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong was restored, Yu Qian and Wang Wen died; Xun was beaten one hundred strokes and banished to guard Tieling.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong was restored to the throne, Yu Qian and Wang Wen were put to death; Chen Xun received one hundred strokes of the cane and was exiled to Tieling Guard.

sentences.zh: 循在宣德時，御史張楷獻詩忤旨。

translations.literal: When Xun was in the Xuande period, the censor Zhang Kai presented a poem that offended the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuande reign, when censor Zhang Kai presented a poem that offended the emperor,

sentences.zh: 循曰「彼亦忠愛也」，遂得釋。

translations.literal: Xun said, "He too acts from loyal devotion," and Zhang was released.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun said, "He too is moved by loyal devotion," and Zhang was released.

sentences.zh: 御史陳祚上疏，觸帝怒，循婉為解，得不死。

translations.literal: The censor Chen Zuo submitted a memorial that provoked the emperor's anger; Xun tactfully interceded and Chen was spared death.
translations.idiomatic: When censor Chen Zuo submitted a memorial that enraged the emperor, Chen Xun interceded tactfully and Chen was spared execution.

sentences.zh: 景帝朝，嘗集古帝王行事，名《勤政要典》，上之。

translations.literal: In the Jingtai reign he once compiled the deeds of ancient emperors and kings, titled Essentials of Diligent Governance, and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jingtai Emperor he compiled the deeds of ancient rulers into a work called Essentials of Diligent Governance and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 河南江北大雪，麥苗死，請發帑市麥種給貧民。

translations.literal: When heavy snow in Henan and Jiangbei killed the wheat seedlings, he requested disbursement from the treasury to buy seed wheat for the poor.
translations.idiomatic: When heavy snow in Henan and the region north of the Yangtze killed the wheat crop, he urged that treasury funds be used to buy seed grain for the poor.

sentences.zh: 因事進言，多足采者。

translations.literal: On various occasions he offered advice, much of it worth adopting.
translations.idiomatic: Much of the counsel he offered on current affairs was worth adopting.

sentences.zh: 然久居政地，刻躁為士論所薄。

translations.literal: Yet having long held power, his harsh and irritable character was slighted in scholarly opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet after long years in power his harsh and irritable temper earned him contempt among the literati.

sentences.zh: 其嚴譴則石亨輩為之，非帝意也。

translations.literal: His severe punishment was the work of Shi Heng and his faction, not the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: His harsh punishment was chiefly the work of Shi Heng and his faction, not the emperor's own wish.

sentences.zh: 亨等既敗，循自貶所上書自訟，言：「天位，陛下所固有。

translations.literal: After Heng and the others fell, Xun from his place of demotion submitted a memorial pleading his case, saying: "The heavenly throne is Your Majesty's by inherent right.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Heng's faction fell, Chen Xun wrote from exile to plead his case: "The throne is Your Majesty's by right.

sentences.zh: 當天與人歸之時，群臣備法駕大樂，恭詣南內，奏請臨朝。

translations.literal: When heaven and men returned to you, the ministers should have prepared the imperial carriage and great music, respectfully gone to the Southern Palace, and requested Your Majesty to preside at court.
translations.idiomatic: When heaven and the people turned back to you, the ministers should have brought out the imperial carriage and ceremonial music, gone respectfully to the Southern Palace, and asked you to resume the throne.

sentences.zh: 非特宮禁不驚，抑亦可示天下萬世。

translations.literal: This would not only have kept the palace untroubled but also shown the realm for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: That would not only have kept the palace calm but would have set an example for all posterity.

sentences.zh: 而亨等僥倖一時，計不出此，卒皆自取禍敗。

translations.literal: Yet Heng and the others grasped at momentary advantage and devised nothing of this sort; in the end they all brought ruin on themselves.
translations.idiomatic: But Shi Heng and his followers seized a moment's advantage and never conceived such a plan; in the end they brought ruin on themselves.

sentences.zh: 臣服事累葉，曾著微勞，實為所擠，惟陛下憐察。

translations.literal: Your servant has served through successive reigns and once rendered slight service; I was in truth squeezed out—may Your Majesty pity and examine.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has served through several reigns and once rendered modest service; I was in truth forced out—may Your Majesty look upon me with compassion.

sentences.zh: 」詔釋為民，一年卒。

translations.literal: " An edict released him to commoner status; a year later he died.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict restored him to commoner status; he died a year later.

sentences.zh: 成化中，于謙事雪，循子引例請恤，乃復官賜祭。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua period, when Yu Qian's case was cleared, Xun's son cited precedent to request posthumous favor; his office was restored and sacrifices were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chenghua reign, after Yu Qian's name was cleared, Chen Xun's son cited precedent to seek posthumous honors; Chen's office was restored and imperial sacrifices were granted.

sentences.zh: 同邑蕭鎡。

translations.literal: Xiao Zi of the same district.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zi, a fellow townsman.

sentences.zh: 字孟勤。

translations.literal: Styled Mengqin.
translations.idiomatic: His style name was Mengqin.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年進士，需次於家。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate of the second year of Xuande, he awaited appointment at home.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in 1427 and waited at home for appointment.

sentences.zh: 八年，帝命楊溥合選三科進士，拔二十八人為庶吉士，鎡為首。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the emperor ordered Yang Pu jointly to select graduates of three examinations, chose twenty-eight as Hanlin bachelor, and Zi ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: In 1433 the emperor ordered Yang Pu to select graduates from three examination cycles; twenty-eight were chosen as Hanlin bachelors, with Xiao Zi at the head of the list.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，授編修。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong acceded, he was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong acceded, he was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 正統三年進侍讀。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengtong he was promoted to reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In 1438 he was promoted to reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 久之，代李時勉為國子監祭酒。

translations.literal: After a long while he replaced Li Shimian as chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he succeeded Li Shimian as chancellor of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年以老疾辭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai he resigned on grounds of age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1450 he resigned citing age and illness.

sentences.zh: 既得允，監丞鮑相率六館生連章乞留。

translations.literal: Once permission was granted, the assistant director Bao Xiang led students of the six halls in successive memorials begging him to stay.
translations.idiomatic: Once his resignation was approved, assistant director Bao Xiang led students from all six halls in joint memorials asking that he be retained.

sentences.zh: 帝可其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor approved their memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted their request.

sentences.zh: 明年以本官兼翰林學士，與侍郎王一寧並入直文淵閣。

translations.literal: The next year, in his original post he also became Hanlin academician and with Vice Minister Wang Yining entered service in the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was also made Hanlin academician and, together with Vice Minister Wang Yining, entered regular duty in the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 又明年進戶部右侍郎，兼官如故。

translations.literal: The year after he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue, his concurrent posts unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue while keeping his other posts.

sentences.zh: 易儲議起，鎡曰：「無易樹子，霸者所禁，矧天朝乎。

translations.literal: When the proposal to change the heir arose, Zi said: "Do not replace the established heir—hegemons forbade it, how much more the celestial dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: When debate arose over replacing the heir apparent, Xiao Zi said: "Do not displace the established heir—hegemons forbade it; how much more should the Son of Heaven's house.

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: " He was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: " His counsel went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 加太子少師。

translations.literal: He was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 《寰宇通志》成，進戶部尚書。

translations.literal: When the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Realm was completed, he was promoted to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Realm was completed, he was promoted to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 帝不豫，諸臣議復憲宗東宮。

translations.literal: When the emperor fell ill, the ministers deliberated restoring the Eastern Palace of Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill, the ministers debated restoring the future Chenghua Emperor as heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 李賢私問鎡，鎡曰：「既退，不可再也。

translations.literal: Li Xian privately asked Zi; Zi said: "Once removed, one cannot be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian asked him privately; Xiao Zi replied, "Once deposed, an heir cannot be restored.

sentences.zh: 」英宗復位，遂削籍。

translations.literal: " When Emperor Yingzong was restored, he was struck from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: " When Emperor Yingzong was restored, Xiao Zi was struck from the official rolls.

sentences.zh: 天順八年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the eighth year of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1464.

sentences.zh: 成化中，復官賜祭。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua period his office was restored and sacrifices were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chenghua reign his office was restored and imperial sacrifices were granted.

sentences.zh: 鎡學問該博，文章爾雅。

translations.literal: Zi's learning was comprehensive and his writing refined.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zi's learning was broad and his prose elegant.

sentences.zh: 然性猜忌，遇事多退避雲。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was suspicious and jealous; in affairs he often drew back.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was suspicious by nature and habitually shrank from confrontation.

sentences.zh: 王文，字千之，初名強，束鹿人。

translations.literal: Wang Wen, styled Qianzhi, originally named Qiang, was a native of Shulu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wen, whose style name was Qianzhi and whose original name was Qiang, came from Shulu.

sentences.zh: 永樂十九年進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate of the nineteenth year of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in 1421.

sentences.zh: 授監察御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 持廉奉法，為都御史顧佐所稱。

translations.literal: Upholding integrity and observing the law, he was praised by the censor-in-chief Gu Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: He upheld integrity and the law and won praise from Censor-in-Chief Gu Zuo.

sentences.zh: 宣德末，奉命治彰德妖賊張普祥獄。

translations.literal: At the end of Xuande he was ordered to handle the case of the Zhangde sorcerer-rebel Zhang Puxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Xuande reign he was ordered to try the sorcerer-rebel Zhang Puxiang of Zhangde.

sentences.zh: 還奏稱旨，賜今名。

translations.literal: On his return his memorial pleased the emperor and he was granted his present name.
translations.idiomatic: His report on returning pleased the emperor, who granted him his present name.

sentences.zh: 景泰改元，召掌院事。

translations.literal: When the reign title changed to Jingtai he was summoned to head the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingtai reign began, he was summoned to head the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 文為人深刻有城府，面目嚴冷，與陳鎰同官，一揖外未嘗接談。

translations.literal: Wen was by nature deep and scheming, his countenance stern and cold; serving with Chen Yi, beyond a single bow he never conversed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wen was deep and calculating, his face stern and cold; though he served alongside Chen Yi, beyond a single bow he never spoke with him.

sentences.zh: 諸御史畏之若神，廷臣無敢幹以私者，然中實柔媚。

translations.literal: The censors feared him as a spirit; court ministers dared not approach him with private requests, yet inwardly he was in truth soft and fawning.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinate censors feared him like a god; no courtier dared approach him for private favor, yet inwardly he was servile and fawning.

sentences.zh: 初，按大理少卿薛瑄獄，希王振指，欲坐瑄死。

translations.literal: At first, investigating the case of the Dali Vice Minister Xue Xuan, he followed Wang Zhen's intent and sought to convict Xuan to death.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while investigating Vice Minister of Justice Xue Xuan, he had followed Wang Zhen's wishes and tried to have Xue condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 至是治中官金英縱家奴不法事，但抵奴罪。

translations.literal: Now, handling the eunuch Jin Ying's allowing his household slaves to break the law, he punished only the slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Now, when the eunuch Jin Ying's household slaves broke the law, he punished only the slaves.

sentences.zh: 給事中林聰等劾文、鎰畏勢長奸，下詔獄。

translations.literal: The supervising secretaries Lin Cong and others impeached Wen and Yi for fearing power and abetting wrong; they were sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries led by Lin Cong impeached Wang Wen and Chen Yi for bowing to power and abetting wrongdoing; both were sent to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 二人俱伏，乃宥之。

translations.literal: Both men confessed and were then pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Both confessed and were then pardoned.

sentences.zh: 二年六月，學士江淵上言法司斷獄多枉。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year the academician Jiang Yuan memorialized that the judiciary often wrongly judged cases.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year Academician Jiang Yuan memorialized that the judiciary often rendered unjust verdicts.

sentences.zh: 文及刑部尚書俞士悅求罷。

translations.literal: Wen and the Minister of Justice Yu Shiyue requested dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wen and Minister of Justice Yu Shiyue asked to be relieved of office.

sentences.zh: 且言淵嘗私以事，不聽，故見誣。

translations.literal: They also said Yuan had once privately asked them favors, which they refused, and therefore he slandered them.
translations.idiomatic: They also claimed that Jiang Yuan had once sought private favors from them, which they had refused, and that he now slandered them for that reason.

sentences.zh: 帝兩置之。

translations.literal: The emperor set both matters aside.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took no action on either side.

sentences.zh: 三年春，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時陳鎰鎮陜西，將還，文當代。

translations.literal: At that time Chen Yi was commanding Shaanxi and about to return; Wen was to succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chen Yi was commanding Shaanxi and was about to return; Wang Wen was to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 諸御史交章留之，乃改命侍郎耿九疇。

translations.literal: The censors submitted successive memorials to retain him; the appointment was then changed to Vice Minister Geng Jiuchou.
translations.idiomatic: The censors submitted joint memorials asking that he stay, and the court instead appointed Vice Minister Geng Jiuchou.

sentences.zh: 南京地震，江、淮北大水，命巡視。

translations.literal: When Nanjing suffered an earthquake and the Jianghuai region north of the Yangtze great floods, he was ordered to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: After an earthquake at Nanjing and great floods on the Jianghuai plain, he was ordered to tour the affected regions.

sentences.zh: 偕南九卿議上軍民便宜九事。

translations.literal: Together with the nine ministers of the south he deliberated and presented nine measures of convenience for soldiers and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: Together with the nine chief ministers of the southern capital he proposed nine relief measures for soldiers and civilians.

sentences.zh: 又言徐、淮間饑甚，而南京儲蓄有余，請盡發徐、淮倉粟振貸，而以應輸南京者輸徐、淮，補其缺。

translations.literal: He also said that between Xuzhou and the Huai region famine was severe while Nanjing's stores were ample; he requested that all grain in the Xuzhou and Huai granaries be released for relief loans, and that grain due to Nanjing be sent to Xuzhou and the Huai instead to make up the shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported severe famine between Xuzhou and the Huai while Nanjing's granaries were full, and urged that all grain in the Xuzhou and Huai stores be released for relief loans, with grain destined for Nanjing redirected to Xuzhou and the Huai to cover the gap.

sentences.zh: 皆報可。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of these proposals.

sentences.zh: 是時，陳循最任，好剛自用。

translations.literal: At this time Chen Xun held the greatest trust and was fond of stubborn self-will.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Chen Xun held the greatest influence and was stubborn and self-willed.

sentences.zh: 高谷與循不相能，以文強悍，思引與共政以敵之，乃疏請增閣員。

translations.literal: Gao Gu could not get along with Xun; considering Wen fierce and strong, he wished to bring him in to share power to oppose Xun and memorialized to increase Grand Secretariat members.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gu was at odds with Chen Xun; seeing Wang Wen as forceful and aggressive, he hoped to bring him into the Grand Secretariat to counter Xun and memorialized to add a seat.

sentences.zh: 循舉其鄉人蕭維禎，谷遂舉文。

translations.literal: Xun recommended his fellow townsman Xiao Weizhen; Gu then recommended Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun recommended his fellow townsman Xiao Weizhen, and Gao Gu in turn recommended Wang Wen.

sentences.zh: 而文得中官王誠助，於是詔用文。

translations.literal: Wen obtained the help of the eunuch Wang Cheng, and an edict appointed Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wen won support from the eunuch Wang Cheng, and an edict appointed him.

sentences.zh: 尋自江、淮還朝，改吏部尚書，兼翰林院學士，直文淵閣。

translations.literal: Soon returning from the Jianghuai to court, he was made Minister of Personnel, concurrently Hanlin academician, serving in the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after returning from the Jianghuai tour he was made Minister of Personnel and Hanlin academician with regular duty in the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 二品大臣入閣自文始。

translations.literal: A second-rank minister entering the Grand Secretariat began with Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wen was the first second-rank minister to enter the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋遭母喪，奪哀如前。

translations.literal: Soon he suffered his mother's death and, as before, was compelled to leave mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He soon lost his mother and, as before, was ordered back to office without completing mourning.

sentences.zh: 文雖為谷所引，而谷遲重，循性明決，文反與循合而不附谷。

translations.literal: Although Wen had been brought in by Gu, Gu was slow and weighty while Xun was clear and decisive; Wen instead aligned with Xun and did not attach himself to Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Though Gao Gu had brought Wang Wen in, Gao was slow and ponderous while Chen Xun was sharp and decisive; Wang Wen sided with Chen Xun instead of Gao Gu.

sentences.zh: 其後以子倫故，欲傾考官，又用谷言而罷。

translations.literal: Later, because of his son Lun, he wished to ruin the examiners but again followed Gu's words and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on account of his son Lun, he tried to bring down the examiners but again heeded Gao Gu and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 由是兩人卒不相得。

translations.literal: From this the two men never got along in the end.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the two men never reconciled.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，江、淮大水，復命巡視。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year great floods struck the Jianghuai; he was again ordered to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year great floods struck the Jianghuai, and he was again ordered to tour the region.

sentences.zh: 先是蘇、松、常、鎮四府糧四石折白銀一兩，民以為便。

translations.literal: Previously the four prefectures Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, and Zhenjiang had converted four piculs of grain to one tael of white silver, which the people found convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the four prefectures of Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, and Zhenjiang had been allowed to pay one tael of silver in lieu of four piculs of grain, which the people found convenient.

sentences.zh: 後戶部復征米，令輸徐、淮，凡一百十余萬石。

translations.literal: Later the Ministry of Revenue again levied grain and ordered delivery to Xuzhou and the Huai, totaling more than 1.1 million piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Ministry of Revenue again demanded grain payment and ordered delivery to Xuzhou and the Huai, more than 1.1 million piculs in all.

sentences.zh: 率三石而致一石，有破家者。

translations.literal: On average three piculs were spent to deliver one; some families were ruined.
translations.idiomatic: It often took three piculs to deliver one, and some families were ruined.

sentences.zh: 文用便宜停之。

translations.literal: Wen used emergency authority to halt it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wen used his discretionary authority to halt the levy.

sentences.zh: 又發廩振饑民三百六十余萬。

translations.literal: He also opened granaries to relieve more than 3.6 million famine sufferers.
translations.idiomatic: He also opened granaries to relieve more than 3.6 million famine sufferers.

sentences.zh: 時年饑多盜，文捕長洲盜許道師等二百人。

translations.literal: Famine that year brought many bandits; Wen arrested more than two hundred bandits of Changzhou led by Xu Daoshi.
translations.idiomatic: Famine that year bred many bandits; Wang Wen arrested more than two hundred Changzhou bandits led by Xu Daoshi.

sentences.zh: 欲張其功，坐以謀逆。

translations.literal: Wishing to magnify his achievement, he charged them with plotting treason.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking to magnify his achievement, he charged them with plotting treason.

sentences.zh: 大理卿薛瑄辨其誣。

translations.literal: The Dali Minister Xue Xuan showed the charge was false.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Xue Xuan showed that the charge was false.

sentences.zh: 給事中王鎮乞會廷臣勘實，得為盜者十六人置之法，而余得釋。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Wang Zhen requested that court ministers jointly investigate; sixteen proved to be bandits were punished by law, and the rest were released.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Wang Zhen asked that court ministers investigate jointly; sixteen were found to be bandits and punished, and the rest were released.

sentences.zh: 還進少保，兼東閣大學士。

translations.literal: On his return he was promoted to Junior Guardian and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was promoted to Junior Guardian and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 再進謹身殿大學士，仍兼東閣。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall, still concurrently of the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall while retaining his Eastern Pavilion post.

sentences.zh: 初，英宗之還也，廷臣議奉迎禮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong first returned, court ministers deliberated the ceremony of welcome.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong first returned from captivity, the court debated the ceremony for welcoming him back.

sentences.zh: 文時為都御史，厲聲曰：「公等謂上皇果還耶？

translations.literal: Wen was then censor-in-chief and said in a harsh voice: "Do you gentlemen think the Retired Emperor will truly return?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wen was then censor-in-chief and said sharply: "Do you really believe the Retired Emperor will come back?

sentences.zh: 也先不索土地、金帛而遽送駕來耶？

translations.literal: Would Esen send the imperial carriage back without demanding land, gold, and silks?"
translations.idiomatic: Would Esen send him back without demanding territory, gold, and silks?"

sentences.zh: 」眾素畏文，皆愕然不決而罷。

translations.literal: All had long feared Wen; they were startled, could not decide, and dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers had long feared Wang Wen; they were stunned, could reach no decision, and dispersed.

sentences.zh: 及易儲議起，文率先承命。

translations.literal: When the proposal to change the heir arose, Wen was first to accept the order.
translations.idiomatic: When debate arose over replacing the heir apparent, Wang Wen was the first to accept the emperor's will.

sentences.zh: 景帝不豫，群臣欲乞還沂王東宮。

translations.literal: When the Jingtai Emperor fell ill, the ministers wished to beg restoration of the Prince of Qi's Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingtai Emperor fell ill, ministers wished to ask that the Prince of Qi's son be restored as heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 文曰：「安知上意誰屬？

translations.literal: Wen said: "How do we know whom the emperor's intent favors?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wen said: "How can we know whom the emperor favors?

sentences.zh: 」乃疏請早選元良。

translations.literal: " He then memorialized requesting early selection of the primary heir.
translations.idiomatic: " He then memorialized urging early selection of a crown prince.

sentences.zh: 以是中外喧傳文與中官王誠等謀召取襄世子。

translations.literal: From this inside and outside the court loudly spread that Wen and the eunuch Wang Cheng and others plotted to summon the heir of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread inside and outside the court that Wang Wen and the eunuch Wang Cheng were plotting to summon the heir of the Prince of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 英宗復位，即日與于謙執於班內。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong was restored, that same day he and Yu Qian were seized within the court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The day Emperor Yingzong was restored, Wang Wen and Yu Qian were seized in the court assembly.

sentences.zh: 言官劾文與謙等謀立外藩，命鞫於廷。

translations.literal: Censorial officials impeached Wen and Qian for plotting to enthrone a foreign prince; they were ordered tried in court.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials impeached Wang Wen and Yu Qian for plotting to enthrone a prince of the frontier; they were ordered tried in open court.

sentences.zh: 文力辯曰：「召親王須用金牌信符，遣人必有馬牌，內府兵部可驗也。

translations.literal: Wen argued forcefully: "Summoning an imperial prince requires the gold tally and credentials; dispatch must have a horse tally—the inner palace and Ministry of War can verify.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wen argued forcefully: "Summoning an imperial prince requires the gold tally and credentials, and any envoy must carry a horse tally—the inner palace and Ministry of War can verify this.

sentences.zh: 」辭氣激壯。

translations.literal: " His words were fierce and bold.
translations.idiomatic: " His manner was fierce and defiant.

sentences.zh: 逮車駕主事沈敬按問，無跡。

translations.literal: When the director of imperial carriages Shen Jing investigated, no trace was found.
translations.idiomatic: When Director of Imperial Carriages Shen Jing investigated, no evidence was found.

sentences.zh: 廷臣遂坐謙、文召敬謀未定，與謙同斬於市，諸子悉戍邊。

translations.literal: The court ministers then convicted Qian and Wen of summoning Jing while the plot was unsettled; Wen was beheaded in the market like Qian, and all his sons were banished to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The court then convicted Yu Qian and Wang Wen of summoning Shen Jing while the plot was still unsettled; Wang Wen was beheaded in the market like Yu Qian, and all his sons were exiled to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 敬亦坐知謀反故縱，減死，戍鐵嶺。

translations.literal: Jing was also convicted of knowing of the treason plot and deliberately allowing it; his death sentence was reduced and he was banished to Tieling.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Jing was also convicted of knowing of the plot and deliberately allowing it; his death sentence was commuted and he was exiled to Tieling.

sentences.zh: 文之死，人皆知其誣。

translations.literal: At Wen's death all knew he had been falsely charged.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone knew Wang Wen's execution was a frame-up.

sentences.zh: 以素刻忮，且迎駕、復儲之議不愜輿論，故冤死而民不思。

translations.literal: Because he had long been harsh and jealous, and because his views on welcoming the emperor and restoring the heir did not satisfy public opinion, though he died unjustly the people did not mourn him.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had long been harsh and jealous, and because his opposition to welcoming the emperor home and restoring the former heir had offended public opinion, though he died unjustly the people did not mourn him.

sentences.zh: 成化初，赦其子還，尋復官，贈太保，謚毅湣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua his son was pardoned and returned; soon his office was restored, he was posthumously made Grand Guardian, and given the posthumous title Yimin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chenghua reign his son was pardoned and allowed to return; Wang Wen's office was soon restored, he was posthumously made Grand Guardian, and given the posthumous title Yimin.

sentences.zh: 倫，改名宗彜。

translations.literal: Lun changed his name to Zongyi.
translations.idiomatic: Lun changed his name to Zongyi.

sentences.zh: 成化初進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate at the beginning of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination early in the Chenghua reign.

sentences.zh: 歷戶部郎中，出理遼東餉。

translations.literal: He served as a director in the Ministry of Revenue and went out to manage Liaodong provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director in the Ministry of Revenue and was sent to manage provisions for Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 中官汪直東征，言宗彜督餉勞，擢太仆少卿。

translations.literal: When the eunuch Wang Zhi campaigned eastward, he said Zongyi's supervision of provisions had been arduous and Zongyi was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Wang Zhi campaigned in the east, he reported Zongyi's arduous work supervising provisions, and Zongyi was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，累官南京禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi period he rose through posts to Minister of Rites at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Hongzhi Emperor he rose to Minister of Rites at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 卒，謚安簡。

translations.literal: He died and was given the posthumous title Anjian.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Anjian.

sentences.zh: 江淵，字世用，江津人。

translations.literal: Jiang Yuan, styled Shiyong, was a native of Jiangjin.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yuan, whose style name was Shiyong, came from Jiangjin.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: A Hanlin bachelor of the fifth year of Xuande, he was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as a Hanlin bachelor in 1430, he was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 正統十二年詔與杜寧、裴綸、劉儼、商輅、陳文、楊鼎、呂原、劉俊、王玉共十人，肄業東閣，曹鼐等為之師。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhengtong an edict ordered him with Du Ning, Pei Lun, Liu Yan, Shang Lu, Chen Wen, Yang Ding, Lü Yuan, Liu Jun, and Wang Yu—ten in all—to study in the Eastern Pavilion, with Cao Qi and others as their teachers.
translations.idiomatic: In 1447 an edict named him with Du Ning, Pei Lun, Liu Yan, Shang Lu, Chen Wen, Yang Ding, Lü Yuan, Liu Jun, and Wang Yu—ten in all—to study in the Eastern Pavilion under Cao Qi and others.

sentences.zh: 郕王監國，徐有貞倡議南遷，太監金英叱出之，踉蹌過左掖門。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Cheng acted as regent, Xu Youzhen advocated moving the capital south; the eunuch Jin Ying shouted him out, and he staggered past the Left Flank Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Cheng acted as regent, Xu Youzhen proposed moving the capital south; the eunuch Jin Ying drove him out, and he staggered past the Left Flank Gate.

sentences.zh: 淵適入，迎問之。

translations.literal: Yuan was just entering and met him to ask.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yuan was just entering and met him to ask what had happened.

sentences.zh: 有貞曰：「以吾議南遷不合也。

translations.literal: Youzhen said: "Because my proposal to move south did not accord with their views.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Youzhen said: "They rejected my proposal to move the capital south.

sentences.zh: 」於是淵入，極陳固守之策。

translations.literal: " Yuan then entered and argued at length for a strategy of firm defense.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiang Yuan then entered and argued at length for holding the capital firm.

sentences.zh: 遂見知於王，由侍講超擢刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He thereby won the prince's trust and was promoted from lecturing reader straight to Right Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He thereby won the prince's trust and was promoted from lecturing reader directly to Right Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 也先薄京師，命淵參都督孫鏜軍事。

translations.literal: When Esen pressed on the capital, Yuan was ordered to assist the regional commander Sun Tang in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen threatened the capital, Jiang Yuan was ordered to assist Regional Commander Sun Tang.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年出視紫荊、倒馬、白羊諸關隘，與都指揮同知翁信督修雁門關。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai he went out to inspect the passes Zijing, Daoma, and Baiyang, and with the regional assistant commander Weng Xin supervised repairs to Yanmen Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In 1450 he inspected the Zijing, Daoma, and Baiyang passes and, with Regional Assistant Commander Weng Xin, supervised repairs to Yanmen Pass.

sentences.zh: 其秋遂以本官兼翰林學士，入閣預機務。

translations.literal: That autumn he was made Hanlin academician in his original post and entered the Grand Secretariat to participate in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was also made Hanlin academician and entered the Grand Secretariat to handle state affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋改戶部侍郎，兼職如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue, his concurrent posts unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue while keeping his other posts.

sentences.zh: 明年六月以天變條上三事：一，厚結朵顏、赤斤諸衛，為東西藩籬；

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the next year, citing heaven's warnings, he listed three matters: first, bind closely the guards Duoyan and Chijin as eastern and western bulwarks;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the following year, citing celestial warnings, he listed three proposals: first, cultivate close ties with the Duoyan and Chijin guards as bulwarks east and west;

sentences.zh: 一，免京軍余丁，以資生業；

translations.literal: second, exempt surplus sons of capital garrison troops so they might support their livelihoods;
translations.idiomatic: second, exempt surplus sons of capital garrison troops so they could pursue livelihoods;

sentences.zh: 一，禁訐告王振余黨，以免枉濫。

translations.literal: third, forbid informers against Wang Zhen's remaining faction to avoid wrongful excess.
translations.idiomatic: third, forbid informers against Wang Zhen's remaining followers to prevent wrongful prosecutions.

sentences.zh: 詔悉從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved all.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved all three.

sentences.zh: 又明年二月改吏部，仍兼學士。

translations.literal: In the second month of the year after he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, still concurrently academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel while retaining his academician title.

sentences.zh: 是春，京師久雨雪。

translations.literal: That spring the capital had long rain and snow.
translations.idiomatic: That spring the capital had prolonged rain and snow.

sentences.zh: 淵上言：「漢劉向曰，凡雨陰也，雪又雨之陰也。

translations.literal: Yuan memorialized: "Liu Xiang of Han said that all rain is yin, and snow is yin within yin.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yuan memorialized: "Liu Xiang of Han said that rain is yin, and snow is yin within yin.

sentences.zh: 仲春少陽用事，而寒氣脅之，占法謂人君刑法暴濫之象。

translations.literal: In mid-spring lesser yang holds sway, yet cold qi presses upon it; prognostication holds this an image of the ruler's punishments violent and excessive.
translations.idiomatic: In mid-spring lesser yang should prevail, yet cold forces press upon it; prognostication treats this as a sign that the ruler's punishments are harsh and excessive.

sentences.zh: 陛下恩威溥洽，未嘗不赦過宥罪，竊恐有司奉行無狀，冤抑或有未伸。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's grace and majesty reach everywhere, and you have never failed to pardon faults and spare guilt; I fear officials may execute orders without proper form and some wrongs may remain unredressed.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's grace and authority reach everywhere, and you have never failed to pardon faults; yet I fear that officials may carry out orders improperly and some injustices may remain unredressed.

sentences.zh: 且向者下明詔，免景泰二年田租之三。

translations.literal: Moreover you recently issued a clear edict exempting one-third of the Jingtai second-year land tax.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover you recently issued a clear edict exempting one-third of the second-year Jingtai land tax.

sentences.zh: 今復移檄追征，則是朝廷自失大信於民。

translations.literal: Now urgent orders again pursue collection; this is the court itself breaking great faith with the people.
translations.idiomatic: Now urgent orders pursue collection again; the court itself is breaking faith with the people.

sentences.zh: 怨氣郁結，良由此也。

translations.literal: Resentment pent up—truly it stems from this.
translations.idiomatic: Popular resentment has built up largely for this reason.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃令法司申冤濫，詰戶部違詔，下尚書金濂於獄，卒免稅加詔。

translations.literal: " The emperor then ordered the judiciary to review wrongful cases, rebuked the Ministry of Revenue for violating the edict, imprisoned Minister Jin Lian, and in the end exempted the tax and added a proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then ordered the judiciary to review wrongful cases, rebuked the Ministry of Revenue for violating the edict, imprisoned Minister Jin Lian, and in the end exempted the tax and issued a further proclamation.

sentences.zh: 東宮既易，加太子少師。

translations.literal: After the Eastern Palace was changed, he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After the heir apparent was replaced, he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 四川巡撫僉都御史李匡不職，以淵言罷之。

translations.literal: The Sichuan grand coordinator and vice censor-in-chief Li Kuang was derelict; on Yuan's word he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan Grand Coordinator Li Kuang was derelict in duty and was dismissed on Jiang Yuan's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 母憂起復。

translations.literal: He left mourning for his mother and was recalled to office.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled from mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 初侍講學士倪謙遭喪，淵薦謙為講官，謙遂奪哀。

translations.literal: Earlier when lecturing academician Ni Qian suffered bereavement, Yuan recommended Qian as lecturer; Qian was then compelled to leave mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when lecturing academician Ni Qian was in mourning, Jiang Yuan had recommended him as lecturer, and Ni Qian was then compelled to leave mourning.

sentences.zh: 至是御史周文言淵引謙，正自為今日地。

translations.literal: Now the censor Zhou Wen said Yuan had brought in Qian precisely to prepare for this day.
translations.idiomatic: Now censor Zhou Wen said Jiang Yuan had brought in Ni Qian precisely to prepare for his own recall today.

sentences.zh: 帝以事既處分，不問，而令自今群臣遭喪無濫保。

translations.literal: The emperor, since the matter had already been handled, did not inquire further but ordered that from now on when ministers suffered bereavement there should be no indiscriminate guarantees.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, since the matter had already been settled, took no further action but ordered that henceforth no minister in mourning should be indiscriminately recommended back to office.

sentences.zh: 五年春，山東、河南、江北饑，命同平江侯陳預往撫。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year Shandong, Henan, and Jiangbei suffered famine; he was ordered with the Marquis of Pingjiang Chen Yu to go and relieve.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year Shandong, Henan, and the region north of the Yangtze suffered famine; he was ordered to go with the Marquis of Pingjiang Chen Yu to provide relief.

sentences.zh: 淵前後條上軍民便宜十數事。

translations.literal: Yuan before and after listed more than ten measures of convenience for soldiers and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yuan proposed more than ten relief measures for soldiers and civilians.

sentences.zh: 並請築淮安月城以護常盈倉，廣徐州東城以護廣運倉。

translations.literal: He also requested building Huai'an's moon wall to protect the Changying granary and expanding Xuzhou's eastern wall to protect the Guangyun granary.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that Huai'an's outer wall be built to protect the Changying granary and Xuzhou's eastern wall expanded to protect the Guangyun granary.

sentences.zh: 悉議行。

translations.literal: All were deliberated and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved and carried out.

sentences.zh: 時江北洊饑，淮安糧運在塗者，淵悉追還備振，漕卒乘機侵耗。

translations.literal: Famine recurred in Jiangbei; grain transport at Huai'an still on the road Yuan ordered all recalled for relief stores; transport soldiers seized the chance to embezzle and waste.
translations.idiomatic: Famine recurred on the northern bank; Jiang Yuan ordered all grain still in transit at Huai'an recalled for relief, and transport soldiers took the chance to embezzle supplies.

sentences.zh: 事聞，遣御史按實。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, a censor was sent to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was reported, a censor was sent to investigate.

sentences.zh: 淵被劾。

translations.literal: Yuan was impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yuan was impeached.

sentences.zh: 當削籍。

translations.literal: He should have been struck from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: He should have been struck from the official rolls.

sentences.zh: 廷臣以淵守便宜，不當罪。

translations.literal: Court ministers held that Yuan had upheld emergency measures and should not be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers held that Jiang Yuan had acted within his discretionary authority and should not be punished.

sentences.zh: 帝宥之。

translations.literal: The emperor pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 閣臣既不相協，而陳循、王文尤刻私。

translations.literal: The grand secretaries already did not cooperate, and Chen Xun and Wang Wen were especially harsh and selfish.
translations.idiomatic: The grand secretaries already failed to cooperate, and Chen Xun and Wang Wen were especially harsh and self-serving.

sentences.zh: 淵好議論，每為同官所抑，意忽忽不樂。

translations.literal: Yuan loved debate and was often suppressed by his colleagues; his mind grew restless and unhappy.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yuan loved to debate policy and was often overruled by his colleagues; he grew restless and unhappy.

sentences.zh: 會兵部尚書于謙以病在告，詔推一人協理部事。

translations.literal: When Minister of War Yu Qian was on sick leave, an edict ordered recommendation of one person to assist in ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of War Yu Qian took sick leave, an edict called for someone to assist in ministry affairs.

sentences.zh: 淵心欲得之。

translations.literal: Yuan inwardly wished to obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yuan hoped to get the post.

sentences.zh: 循等佯推淵，而密令商輅草奏，示以「石兵江工」四字，淵在旁不知也。

translations.literal: Xun and the others pretended to recommend Yuan but secretly had Shang Lu draft the memorial, showing him the four characters "Shi Bing Jiang Gong"; Yuan beside them did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun and the others pretended to recommend Jiang Yuan but secretly had Shang Lu draft the memorial with the code "Shi Bing Jiang Gong"—transfer Shi to War, Jiang to Works—while Jiang Yuan stood by unaware.

sentences.zh: 比詔下，調工部尚書石璞於兵部，而以淵代璞。

translations.literal: When the edict came down, Minister of Works Shi Pu was transferred to the Ministry of War and Yuan replaced Pu.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, Minister of Works Shi Pu was transferred to the Ministry of War and Jiang Yuan replaced him at Works.

sentences.zh: 淵大失望。

translations.literal: Yuan was greatly disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yuan was deeply disappointed.

sentences.zh: 英宗復位，與陳循等俱謫戍遼東，未幾卒。

translations.literal: When the Ying Emperor was restored to the throne, together with Chen Xun and others he was all banished to garrison Liaodong; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong regained the throne, Jiang Yuan was exiled with Chen Xun and others to serve as a garrison soldier in Liaodong; he died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 初，黃矰之奏易儲也，或疑淵主之。

translations.literal: At the beginning, regarding Huang Kan's memorial to change the stored heir, some suspected Yuan had presided over it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Huang Kan submitted his memorial proposing a change of crown prince, some had suspected that Jiang Yuan was behind it.

sentences.zh: 丘浚曰：「此易辨也，廣西紙與京師紙異。

translations.literal: Qiu Jun said: "This is easy to distinguish; Guangxi paper and capital paper differ."
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Jun said, "This is easy to tell apart—the paper from Guangxi is not the same as paper from the capital."

sentences.zh: 」索奏視之，果廣西紙，其誣乃白。

translations.literal: They sought the memorial to view it; it was indeed Guangxi paper, and the false accusation was then made clear.
translations.idiomatic: They demanded the memorial for inspection; it proved to be Guangxi paper, and the slander against Jiang Yuan was cleared.

sentences.zh: 成化初，復官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua, his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chenghua reign his official rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 許彬，字道中，寧陽人。

translations.literal: Xu Bin, style name Daozhong, was a man of Ningyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Bin, courtesy name Daozhong, was a native of Ningyang.

sentences.zh: 永樂十三年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongle he became a presented scholar.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in 1415.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin bachelor and appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a Hanlin bachelor-at-large and appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 正統末，累遷太常少卿，兼翰林待詔，提督四夷館。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengtong, through repeated promotion he became Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, concurrently Hanlin attendant drafter, supervising the Four Barbarians Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Zhengtong reign he rose through repeated promotions to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, concurrently Hanlin attendant drafter, with charge of the Four Barbarians Institute.

sentences.zh: 上皇將還，遣彬至宣府奉迎。

translations.literal: When the retired emperor was about to return, Bin was sent to Xuanfu to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When the captive emperor was about to return, Xu Bin was dispatched to Xuanfu to receive him.

sentences.zh: 上皇命書罪己詔及諭群臣敕，遣祭土木陣亡官軍。

translations.literal: The retired emperor ordered him to draft the self-reproach edict and an instruction to the ministers, and sent him to sacrifice to the officers and soldiers who died at Tumu.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor had him draft the self-reproach edict and an edict instructing the ministers, and sent him to offer sacrifices for the officers and soldiers killed at Tumu.

sentences.zh: 以此受知上皇。

translations.literal: By this he gained the retired emperor's knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: In this way he won the retired emperor's trust.

sentences.zh: 還擢本寺卿。

translations.literal: On returning he was promoted to chief minister of that temple.
translations.idiomatic: After his return he was promoted to chief minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 石亨等謀復上皇，以其謀告彬，彬進徐有貞，語具有貞傳。

translations.literal: Shi Heng and others plotted to restore the retired emperor; they told their plot to Bin, who advanced Xu Youzhen—the account is in the biography of Xu Youzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Heng and others plotted to restore the retired emperor; they confided their plan to Xu Bin, who introduced Xu Youzhen—the full story is told in Xu Youzhen's biography.

sentences.zh: 英宗復位，進禮部左侍郎，兼翰林院學士。

translations.literal: When the Ying Emperor was restored, he was advanced to Left Vice Minister of Rites, concurrently Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong regained the throne, Xu Bin was promoted to left vice minister of rites, concurrently Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 入直文淵閣。

translations.literal: He entered duty at the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He took up regular duty in the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為石亨所忌，出為南京禮部右侍郎，甫行，貶陜西參政。

translations.literal: Before long, envied by Shi Heng, he was sent out as Right Vice Minister of Rites at Nanjing; scarcely had he set out when he was demoted to administrative vice commissioner in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shi Heng came to resent him; Xu Bin was posted out as right vice minister of rites at Nanjing, and scarcely had he departed when he was demoted to administrative vice commissioner in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 至則乞休去。

translations.literal: On arriving he begged to retire and left.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived he petitioned to retire and withdrew from office.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，命以侍郎致仕，尋卒。

translations.literal: When Xianzong acceded, he was ordered to retire with vice-minister rank; soon after he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong came to the throne, Xu Bin was permitted to retire with the rank of vice minister; he died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 彬性坦率，好交遊，不能擇人，一時浮蕩士多出其門。

translations.literal: Bin was frank and open by nature, fond of socializing, unable to choose men, and many flighty scholars of the time issued from his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Bin was candid by nature and loved company; he could not choose his associates, and many restless men of letters of the day passed through his door.

sentences.zh: 晚參大政，方欲杜門謝客，而客惡其變態，競相騰謗，竟不安其位。

translations.literal: Late in life he entered great policy; just as he wished to shut his door and decline guests, those guests hated his change of manner and competed in spreading slanders, and in the end he could not keep his place secure.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he entered high politics; just as he tried to shut his door to visitors, those guests resented his change of ways and vied in spreading slander, and in the end he could not hold his position.

sentences.zh: 景泰二年，閣臣高谷薦文才，遂擢雲南右布政使，貴州比歲用兵，資餉雲南，民困轉輸。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingtai, Grand Secretary Gao Gu recommended Wen's literary talent, and he was thereupon promoted to Right Administration Commissioner of Yunnan; Guizhou had used troops year after year, supplies were drawn from Yunnan, and the people were distressed by transport.
translations.idiomatic: In 1451 Grand Secretary Gao Gu recommended Chen Wen for his literary talent, and Chen was promoted to right administration commissioner of Yunnan; Guizhou had seen fighting year after year, and because supplies were drawn from Yunnan the people were worn down by transport duties.

sentences.zh: 文令商賈代輸，而民倍償其費，皆稱便。

translations.literal: Wen ordered merchants to deliver in place of transport, while the people reimbursed them double the cost—all called it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wen had merchants deliver supplies in lieu of the people, while the people paid them double the cost in return—everyone pronounced the arrangement convenient.

sentences.zh: 稅課額鈔七十余萬，吏俸所取給，典者侵蝕，吏或累歲不得俸。

translations.literal: The tax quota amounted to over seven hundred thousand in paper notes, from which clerks' salaries were paid; those in charge embezzled, and clerks sometimes went years without salary.
translations.idiomatic: The tax quota ran to more than seven hundred thousand paper notes, from which clerks' salaries were drawn; the officials in charge skimmed funds, and some clerks went years without pay.

sentences.zh: 文悉按治，課日羨溢。

translations.literal: Wen investigated everything thoroughly, and the levies daily grew abundant in surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wen prosecuted every abuse, and the tax receipts daily grew ever more ample.

sentences.zh: 雲南產銀，民間用銀貿易，視內地三倍。

translations.literal: Yunnan produced silver; the people used silver in trade at three times the rate of the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan produced silver, and the people traded in silver at three times the rate used in the interior.

sentences.zh: 隸在官者免役，納銀亦三之，納者不為病。

translations.literal: Bond servants in official households were exempt from corvée labor; silver paid in lieu was also at triple rate, and those who paid were not burdened.
translations.idiomatic: Bond servants attached to officials were exempt from corvée, and the silver substitute levy was likewise tripled—yet those who paid did not find it onerous.

sentences.zh: 文曰：「雖如是，得無傷廉乎？

translations.literal: Wen said: "Even so, may this not harm integrity?"
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wen said, "Even so, does this not compromise our integrity?"

sentences.zh: 」損之，復令減隸額三之一。

translations.literal: He reduced it, and again ordered that the bond-servant quota be cut by one third.
translations.idiomatic: He lowered the levy and again ordered the bond-servant quota reduced by one third.

sentences.zh: 名譽日起，遷廣東左布政使，母憂未赴。

translations.literal: His reputation rose day by day; he was transferred to Left Administration Commissioner of Guangdong but had not taken up the post owing to mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation rose daily; he was transferred to left administration commissioner of Guangdong but had not yet taken up the post because he was in mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 英宗即復位，一日謂左右曰：「向侍朕編修，皙而長者安在？

translations.literal: As soon as the Ying Emperor was restored, one day he said to those beside him: "The reviser who once attended me, fair-skinned and tall—where is he now?"
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Emperor Yingzong regained the throne, one day he asked those around him, "Where is that fair-skinned, tall reviser who once attended me?"

sentences.zh: 」左右以文對，即召為詹事。

translations.literal: Those beside him answered with Wen's name; he was immediately summoned as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Those around him named Chen Wen; the emperor at once summoned him to be grand preceptor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 乞終制。

translations.literal: He begged to complete the mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wen asked to complete his period of mourning.

sentences.zh: 不允。

translations.literal: This was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 入侍東宮講讀。

translations.literal: He entered to serve at the Eastern Palace in lecture and reading.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Eastern Palace to lecture and read with the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 學士呂原卒，帝問李賢誰可代者，曰：「柯潛可。

translations.literal: Academician Lü Yuan died; the emperor asked Li Xian who could replace him, and he said: "Ke Qian will do."
translations.idiomatic: When Academician Lü Yuan died, the emperor asked Li Xian who could replace him; Li said, "Ke Qian would serve."

sentences.zh: 」出告王翺，翺曰：「陳文以次當及，奈何抑之？

translations.literal: Going out he told Wang Ao; Ao said: "Chen Wen by seniority ought to be reached—why suppress him?"
translations.idiomatic: On leaving he told Wang Ao, who said, "Chen Wen should be next in line by seniority—why pass him over?"

sentences.zh: 」明日，賢入見，如翺言。

translations.literal: The next day Xian entered audience and spoke as Ao had said.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Li Xian entered audience and spoke as Wang Ao had urged.

sentences.zh: 七年二月進禮部右侍郎兼學士，入內閣。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year he was advanced to Right Vice Minister of Rites, concurrently academician, and entered the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventh year of Chenghua he was promoted to right vice minister of rites, concurrently academician, and entered the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 文既入，數撓賢以自異，曰：「吾非若所薦也。

translations.literal: Once Wen had entered, he repeatedly thwarted Xian to set himself apart, saying: "I am not one whom you recommended."
translations.idiomatic: Once Chen Wen had entered the cabinet, he repeatedly crossed Li Xian to distinguish himself, saying, "I am not someone you recommended."

sentences.zh: 」侍讀學士錢溥與文比舍居，交甚歡。

translations.literal: Lecturing Reader-in-Waiting Qian Pu lived in neighboring quarters with Wen and were on very friendly terms.
translations.idiomatic: Lecturing reader-in-waiting Qian Pu lived next door to Chen Wen, and the two were on very close terms.

sentences.zh: 溥嘗授內侍書。

translations.literal: Pu had once taught palace eunuchs to write.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Pu had once taught palace eunuchs calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 其徒多貴幸，來謁，必邀文共飲。

translations.literal: Many of his pupils were powerful favorites; when they came to call, Wen was always invited to drink with them.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his pupils were powerful favorites at court; whenever they came to visit, Chen Wen was always asked to join them for drink.

sentences.zh: 英宗大漸，東宮內侍王綸私詣溥計事，不召文。

translations.literal: As Yingzong lay critically ill, Eastern Palace eunuch Wang Lun privately visited Pu to plan affairs and did not summon Wen.
translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Yingzong lay near death, Eastern Palace eunuch Wang Lun went privately to Qian Pu to plot affairs and did not summon Chen Wen.

sentences.zh: 文密覘之。

translations.literal: Wen spied on them in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wen watched them in secret.

sentences.zh: 綸言：「帝不豫，東宮納妃，如何？

translations.literal: Lun said: "The emperor is unwell; how about the Eastern Palace taking a consort?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lun said, "The emperor is ill—what if the Eastern Palace takes a consort?"

sentences.zh: 」溥謂：「當奉遺詔行事。

translations.literal: Pu said: "One should act according to the final testament."
translations.idiomatic: Qian Pu replied, "We should act according to the dying emperor's testament."

sentences.zh: 」已而英宗崩，賢當草詔。

translations.literal: Before long Yingzong died; Xian was to draft the proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Emperor Yingzong died, and Li Xian was to draft the accession proclamation.

sentences.zh: 文起奪其筆曰：「無庸，已有草者。

translations.literal: Wen rose and snatched his brush, saying: "No need—there is already a draft."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wen rose, seized his brush, and said, "No need—there is already a draft."

sentences.zh: 」因言綸、溥定計，欲逐賢以溥代之，而以兵部侍郎韓雍代尚書馬昂。

translations.literal: He then reported that Lun and Pu had fixed a plan to drive out Xian and replace him with Pu, and to replace Minister Ma Ang with Vice Minister of War Han Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He then disclosed that Wang Lun and Qian Pu had plotted to drive out Li Xian and install Qian Pu in his place, and to replace Minister of War Ma Ang with Vice Minister Han Yong.

sentences.zh: 賢怒，發其事。

translations.literal: Xian was enraged and exposed the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian was furious and exposed the affair.

sentences.zh: 是時憲宗初立，綸自謂當得司禮，氣張甚。

translations.literal: At that time Xianzong had just acceded; Lun considered that he ought to obtain the Directorate of Ceremonials and was extremely overbearing in manner.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Xianzong had just acceded; Wang Lun believed he would obtain the Directorate of Ceremonials and carried himself with great arrogance.

sentences.zh: 英宗大殮，綸衰服襲貂，帝見而惡之。

translations.literal: At Yingzong's encoffining, Lun wore mourning garb over sable fur; the emperor saw it and detested him.
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor Yingzong's encoffining, Wang Lun wore mourning garments over sable fur; the new emperor saw it and took offense.

sentences.zh: 太監牛玉恐其軋己，因數綸罪，逐之去。

translations.literal: Eunuch Niu Yu feared Lun would crush him and therefore enumerated Lun's crimes until he was driven away.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Niu Yu feared Wang Lun would overpower him and therefore listed his crimes until Wang Lun was driven out.

sentences.zh: 溥謫知順德縣，雍浙江參政。

translations.literal: Pu was demoted to magistrate of Shunde county; Yong to administrative vice commissioner in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Pu was demoted to magistrate of Shunde County; Han Yong to administrative vice commissioner in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 詞所連，順天府尹王福，通政參議趙昂，南寧伯毛榮，都督馬良、馮宗、劉聚，錦衣都指揮僉事門達等皆坐謫。

translations.literal: Those implicated in the words—all were sentenced to demotion: Shuntian prefectural intendant Wang Fu, Secretariat of Transmission assistant policy adviser Zhao Ang, Naning Earl Mao Rong, regional commanders Ma Liang, Feng Zong, and Liu Ju, and Jinyi chief assistant commandant Men Da, among others.
translations.idiomatic: Those implicated in the testimony were all sentenced to demotion: Shuntian prefectural intendant Wang Fu, Secretariat of Transmission assistant policy adviser Zhao Ang, Naning Earl Mao Rong, regional commanders Ma Liang, Feng Zong, and Liu Ju, and Jinyi chief assistant commandant Men Da, among others.

sentences.zh: 雍亦文素所不悅者也。

translations.literal: Yong was also one whom Wen had long disliked.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yong was also someone Chen Wen had long disliked.

sentences.zh: 改吏部左侍郎，同知經筵事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, jointly managing Classic Colloquium affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wen was transferred to left vice minister of personnel, jointly managing Classic Colloquium affairs.

sentences.zh: 文素以才自許，在外頗著績效，士大夫多冀其進用。

translations.literal: Wen had always prided himself on talent; in provincial posts he achieved considerable results, and many scholar-officials hoped he would be advanced to high use.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wen had always prided himself on his talent; in provincial office he achieved notable results, and many scholar-officials hoped he would rise to high office.

sentences.zh: 及居宮端，行事鄙猥。

translations.literal: Once he held the pinnacle of the palace, his conduct was base and vulgar.
translations.idiomatic: Once he stood at the head of government, his conduct proved base and vulgar.

sentences.zh: 既參大政，無所建明。

translations.literal: Having entered great policy, he put forward nothing of merit.
translations.idiomatic: Having entered high politics, he offered nothing of substance.

sentences.zh: 朝退則引賓客故人置酒為曲宴，專務請屬。

translations.literal: After court he would bring in guests and old friends and set out wine for informal feasts, devoted solely to lobbying and patronage.
translations.idiomatic: After court he would gather guests and old friends for convivial drinking, devoting himself entirely to lobbying and patronage.

sentences.zh: 性卞急，遇睚眥怨必報。

translations.literal: By nature he was impatient and touchy; meet the smallest grudge and he must repay it.
translations.idiomatic: He was impatient by nature and nursed every slight; the smallest grudge he had to repay.

sentences.zh: 及賢卒，文益恣意行，名節大喪。

translations.literal: When Xian died, Wen acted all the more willfully, and his reputation and integrity were greatly ruined.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Xian died, Chen Wen acted all the more recklessly, and his reputation and integrity collapsed.

sentences.zh: 歿後，禮部主事陸淵之、御史謝文祥皆疏論文不當得美謚。

translations.literal: After his death, Ministry of Rites registrar Lu Yuanzhi and censor Xie Wenxiang both memorialized that Wen ought not to receive a fine posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: After his death, Ministry of Rites registrar Lu Yuanzhi and censor Xie Wenxiang both memorialized that Chen Wen did not deserve a flattering posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 帝以事已施行，不許。

translations.literal: The emperor held that the matter had already been carried out and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that the matter had already been settled and refused.

sentences.zh: 萬安，安循吉，眉州人。

translations.literal: Wan An, style name Xunji, was a man of Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wan An, courtesy name Xunji, was a native of Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 長身魁顏，眉目如刻畫，外寬而深中。

translations.literal: Tall in stature with a commanding countenance, his brows and eyes as if carved, outwardly genial but inwardly deep.
translations.idiomatic: Tall and imposing in bearing, with brows and eyes cut as if by the chisel, he seemed open outwardly but was deep and calculating within.

sentences.zh: 正統十三年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhengtong he became a presented scholar.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in 1448.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin bachelor and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a Hanlin bachelor-at-large and appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 成化初，屢遷禮部左侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua he was repeatedly promoted to Left Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chenghua reign he rose through repeated promotions to left vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 五年命兼翰林學士，入內閣參機務。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was ordered to serve concurrently as Hanlin academician and entered the Grand Secretariat to participate in secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chenghua he was ordered to serve concurrently as Hanlin academician and entered the Grand Secretariat to deliberate on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 同年生詹事李泰，中官永昌養子也，齒少於安。

translations.literal: His fellow metropolitan graduate of the same year, Grand Preceptor Li Tai, was the adopted son of the eunuch Yongchang and was younger than An in age.
translations.idiomatic: His fellow metropolitan graduate Li Tai, grand preceptor of the heir apparent, was the adopted son of the eunuch Yongchang and younger than Wan An.

sentences.zh: 安兄事之，得其歡。

translations.literal: An treated him as an elder brother would and won his pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Wan An treated him with the deference of a younger brother and won his favor.

sentences.zh: 自為同官，每當遷，必推安出己上。

translations.literal: From the time they were colleagues, whenever promotion was at hand, he always pushed An above himself.
translations.idiomatic: From the time they served together, whenever promotion was discussed Li Tai always put Wan An ahead of himself.

sentences.zh: 至是議簡閣臣，泰復推安曰：「子先之，我不患不至。

translations.literal: At this time when choosing Grand Secretariat members, Tai again pushed An forward, saying: "You go first—I need not worry that I shall not arrive."
translations.idiomatic: When the time came to select Grand Secretariat members, Li Tai again urged Wan An forward, saying, "You go first—I need not fear that I will not follow."

sentences.zh: 」故安得入閣，而泰忽暴病死。

translations.literal: Thus An entered the cabinet, while Tai suddenly died of a sudden illness.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Wan An entered the cabinet, while Li Tai suddenly died of an acute illness.

sentences.zh: 安無學術，既柄用，惟日事請托，結諸閹為內援。

translations.literal: An had no learning; once he held power, he did nothing each day but lobbying, currying favor with eunuchs as inner support.
translations.idiomatic: Wan An had no scholarship; once he held power he did nothing each day but solicit favors, cultivating eunuchs as backers within the palace.

sentences.zh: 時萬貴妃寵冠後宮，安因內侍致殷勤，自稱子侄行。

translations.literal: At that time the Noble Consort Wan dominated the rear palace; An conveyed cordial attentions through inner attendants and called himself their nephew in the family manner.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Noble Consort Wan dominated the inner palace; Wan An sent warm greetings through palace eunuchs and styled himself their nephew by kinship.

sentences.zh: 妃嘗自愧無門閥，聞則大喜，妃弟錦衣指揮通，遂以族屬數過安家。

translations.literal: The consort had once been ashamed of lacking a great clan; on hearing this she was greatly pleased. Her younger brother, Jinyi commander Tong, then visited An's household several times as kin.
translations.idiomatic: The consort had once been ashamed of lacking a great clan; on hearing this she was overjoyed. Her younger brother Wan Tong, a Jinyi commander, then visited the Wan household repeatedly as kin.

sentences.zh: 其妻王氏有母至自博興。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Wang had a mother who arrived from Boxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wan An's wife, Lady Wang, had a mother who came from Boxing.

sentences.zh: 王謂母曰：「向家貧時，以妹為人娣，今安在？

translations.literal: Lady Wang said to her mother: "In former days when our family was poor, we gave my younger sister as a bondservant to someone—where is she now?"
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang asked her mother, "When our family was poor we gave my younger sister away as a bondservant—where is she now?"

sentences.zh: 」母曰：「第憶為四川萬編修者。

translations.literal: Her mother said: "I only remember her being with a Wan, a reviser in Sichuan."
translations.idiomatic: Her mother replied, "I only remember her being with a Wan who was a reviser in Sichuan."

sentences.zh: 」通心疑是安，訪之則安小婦，由是兩家婦日往來。

translations.literal: Tong inwardly suspected it was An; on inquiry it was An's concubine, and from this the two families' wives visited each other daily.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Tong inwardly suspected it was Wan An; on inquiry it proved to be Wan An's concubine, and from then on the two families' wives visited each other daily.

sentences.zh: 通妻著籍禁內，恣出入，安得備知宮中動靜，益自固。

translations.literal: Tong's wife was registered in the forbidden inner quarters and came and went at will; An thus learned all movements within the palace and grew more secure in power.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Tong's wife was registered in the inner palace and came and went freely; Wan An thus learned everything that moved within the palace and grew more secure in power.

sentences.zh: 侍郎刑讓、祭酒陳鑒與安同年不相能。

translations.literal: Vice Ministers Xing Rang and Libationer Chen Jian were fellow graduates of the same year as An and got along poorly with him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Xing Rang and libationer Chen Jian were Wan An's fellow graduates and were on bad terms with him.
