sentences.zh: 安構獄，除兩人名。

translations.literal: An fabricated prosecutions and removed both men's names.
translations.idiomatic: Wan An fabricated prosecutions and struck both men's names from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 七年冬，彗見天田，犯太微。

translations.literal: In winter of the seventh year a comet appeared in the Celestial Field and encroached upon the Supreme Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the seventh year of Chenghua a comet appeared in the Celestial Field constellation and encroached on the Supreme Palace.

sentences.zh: 廷臣多言君臣否隔，宜時召大臣議政。

translations.literal: Court ministers repeatedly said ruler and minister were estranged and that the emperor ought regularly to summon senior ministers to deliberate on government.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers repeatedly urged that ruler and ministers were estranged and that the emperor should regularly summon senior ministers to discuss policy.

sentences.zh: 大學士彭時、商輅力請。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries Peng Shi and Shang Lu pressed the request forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Peng Shi and Shang Lu pressed the request with special force.

sentences.zh: 司禮中官乃約以禦殿日召對，且曰：「初見，情未洽，勿多言，姑俟他日。

translations.literal: Eunuchs of the Directorate of Ceremonials then arranged to summon them for audience on imperial audience days, and said: "At first meeting feelings are not yet close—do not say much; wait for another day."
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs of the Directorate of Ceremonials then agreed to summon them for audience on imperial audience days, but warned, "At the first meeting feelings are not yet close—do not say much; wait for another day."

sentences.zh: 」將入，復約如初。

translations.literal: As they were about to enter, they made the same arrangement as before.
translations.idiomatic: As they were about to enter audience, the eunuchs repeated the same warning.

sentences.zh: 比見，時言天變可畏，帝曰：「已知，卿等宜盡心。

translations.literal: When they had been received, Shi spoke of how heaven's warnings were to be feared; the emperor said: "I already know—you ministers should do your utmost."
translations.idiomatic: When they were received, Peng Shi spoke of how heaven's warnings were to be feared; the emperor said, "I already know—you ministers should do your utmost."

sentences.zh: 」時又言：「昨御史有疏，請減京官俸薪，武臣不免觖望，乞如舊便。

translations.literal: Shi also said: "Yesterday a censor had a memorial requesting a reduction in Beijing officials' salaries; military officers cannot avoid discontent—pray let it remain as before."
translations.idiomatic: Peng Shi also said, "Yesterday a censor memorialized to cut Beijing officials' salaries; military officers cannot avoid resentment—please leave things as they were."

sentences.zh: 」帝可之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 安遂頓首呼萬歲。

translations.literal: An thereupon kowtowed and cried "Long live [the emperor]!"
translations.idiomatic: Wan An thereupon kowtowed and shouted, "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 欲出，時、輅不得已，皆叩頭退。

translations.literal: About to withdraw, Shi and Lu had no choice but all to kowtow and retire.
translations.idiomatic: About to withdraw, Peng Shi and Shang Lu had no choice but to kowtow and retire with him.

sentences.zh: 中官戲朝士曰：「若輩嘗言不召見。

translations.literal: The eunuchs jested to the court gentlemen: "You lot always say you are not summoned to audience."
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs mocked the court officials: "You always complain that you are never summoned to audience."

sentences.zh: 及見，止知呼萬歲耳。

translations.literal: When summoned, you only know to shout 'Long live.'"
translations.idiomatic: Yet once you are summoned, all you know is to shout 'Long live!'"

sentences.zh: 」一時傳笑，謂之「萬歲閣老」。

translations.literal: For a time it was passed about as a jest, and he was called the "Long-Live Grand Secretary."
translations.idiomatic: For a time the story circulated as a joke, and Wan An was nicknamed the "Long-Live Grand Secretary."

sentences.zh: 帝自是不復召見大臣矣。

translations.literal: From this the emperor no longer again summoned great ministers to audience.
translations.idiomatic: From that day forward the emperor never again summoned senior ministers to audience.

sentences.zh: 其後尹直入閣，欲請見帝計事。

translations.literal: Afterward Yin Zhi entered the Grand Secretariat and wished to request an audience with the emperor to plan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yin Zhi joined the Grand Secretariat and sought an audience with the emperor to discuss state business.

sentences.zh: 安止之曰：「往彭公請召對，一語不合，輒叩頭呼萬歲，以此貽笑。

translations.literal: An stopped him, saying: "Formerly Lord Peng requested a summoned audience; one phrase not agreeing, then at once kowtowed and cried 'Long live,' and thereby left a laughingstock."
translations.idiomatic: Wan An dissuaded him, saying, "When Lord Peng once requested a summoned audience, a single remark fell wrong and he at once kowtowed shouting 'Long live the emperor'—and became a laughingstock."

sentences.zh: 今吾輩每事盡言，太監擇而聞之，上無不允者，勝面對多矣。

translations.literal: Now on each matter we speak fully; eunuchs select and report it, and above there is none not granted—far better than face-to-face audience."
translations.idiomatic: "Now we speak freely on every matter; the eunuchs choose what to report, and the throne grants everything—far better than facing the emperor in person."

sentences.zh: 」其容悅不識大體，且善歸過於人如此。

translations.literal: His bearing was pleasing yet he did not know great principle, and moreover was good at shifting blame onto others in this way.
translations.idiomatic: Wan An's manner was affable, but he lacked grasp of larger principle and habitually shifted blame onto others in just this fashion.

sentences.zh: 九年進禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was advanced to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was promoted to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 久之，改戶部。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was moved to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十三年加太子少保，俄改文淵閣大學士。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent; soon after he was made Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he received the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and was soon appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 孝宗出閤，進吏部尚書、謹身殿大學士，尋加太子太保。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong left the inner quarters, he was advanced to Minister of Personnel and Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall; soon he was also made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent Xiaozong left the inner palace, Wan An was promoted to Minister of Personnel and Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall, and soon thereafter named Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時彭時已歿，商輅以忤汪直去，在內閣者劉珝、劉吉。

translations.literal: At that time Peng Shi had already died; Shang Lu had left for opposing Wang Zhi; those in the Grand Secretariat were Liu Xu and Liu Ji.
translations.idiomatic: By then Peng Shi was dead and Shang Lu had been driven out for opposing Wang Zhi; the Grand Secretariat held only Liu Xu and Liu Ji.

sentences.zh: 而安為首輔，與南人相黨附；

translations.literal: But An was chief minister and formed a faction with southerners;
translations.idiomatic: Wan An served as chief minister and banded together with southerners in a faction;

sentences.zh: 珝與尚書尹旻、王越又以北人為黨，互相傾軋。

translations.literal: Xu, together with Ministers Yin Min and Wang Yue, again took northerners as a faction, and the two sides mutually undermined one another.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xu allied with Ministers Yin Min and Wang Yue in a northern faction, and the two camps constantly undermined each other.

sentences.zh: 然珝疏淺而安深鷙，故珝卒不能勝安。

translations.literal: Yet Xu was superficial while An was deep and fierce, so Xu ultimately could not overcome An.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xu was shallow where Wan An was deep and ruthless, and in the end Liu Xu could not prevail over him.

sentences.zh: 十八年，汪直寵衰，言官請罷西廠。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Wang Zhi's favor waned, and remonstrating officials requested that the Western Depot be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, as Wang Zhi's influence faded, censors memorialized to abolish the Western Depot.

sentences.zh: 帝不許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 安具疏再言之，報可，中外頗以是稱安。

translations.literal: An presented a full memorial stating it again; the reply was approval, and within and without the court fairly on this account praised An.
translations.idiomatic: Wan An submitted a detailed memorial repeating the request; the throne approved, and court and country alike praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 《文華大訓》成，進太子太傅、華蓋殿大學士。

translations.literal: When the Great Compendium of Literary Cultivation was completed, he was advanced to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Upon completion of the Great Compendium of Literary Cultivation, he was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall.

sentences.zh: 復進少傅、太子太師，再進少師。

translations.literal: He was again advanced to Junior Tutor and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and again advanced to Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Junior Tutor and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and then again to Junior Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 當是時，朝多秕政，四方災傷日告。

translations.literal: At that time the court had many rotten policies, and calamities and injuries from the four directions were reported daily.
translations.idiomatic: In those years government was riddled with abuses, and reports of disaster and famine arrived daily from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 帝崇信道教，封金闕、玉闕真君為上帝，遣安祭於靈濟宮。

translations.literal: The emperor revered Daoism, enfeoffed the Lords of the Golden and Jade Gates as Supreme Emperor, and sent An to sacrifice at Lingji Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor devoted himself to Daoism, elevated the Lords of the Golden and Jade Gates to the rank of Supreme Emperor, and dispatched Wan An to offer sacrifice at Lingji Palace.

sentences.zh: 而李孜省、鄧常恩方進用，安因彭華潛與結，藉以排異己。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Li Zhisheng and Deng Chang'en were rising in favor; An, through Peng Hua, secretly allied with them and used this to exclude those unlike themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhisheng and Deng Chang'en were then coming into power; Wan An secretly joined them through Peng Hua and used the alliance to purge rivals.

sentences.zh: 於是珝及王恕、馬文升、秦纮、耿裕諸大臣相繼被逐，而華遂由詹事遷吏部侍郎，入內閣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xu, together with Wang Shu, Ma Wensheng, Qin Hong, Geng Yu, and other great ministers, were successively expelled, while Hua then moved from Grand Mentor to Vice Minister of Personnel and entered the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xu, Wang Shu, Ma Wensheng, Qin Hong, Geng Yu, and other leading ministers were driven out one after another, while Peng Hua rose from Grand Mentor to Vice Minister of Personnel and entered the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 朝臣無敢與安牴牾者。

translations.literal: Among court ministers none dared oppose An.
translations.idiomatic: No court minister dared stand against Wan An.

sentences.zh: 華，安福人，大學士時之族弟，舉景泰五年會試第一。

translations.literal: Hua was a man of Anfu, a younger cousin of Grand Secretary Shi; in the metropolitan examination of the fifth year of Jingtai he placed first.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Hua was from Anfu, a younger cousin of Grand Secretary Peng Shi, and had ranked first in the metropolitan examination of Jingtai 5.

sentences.zh: 深刻多計數，善陰伺人短，與安、孜省比。

translations.literal: Deep and cutting, full of stratagems, skilled at secretly watching others' faults—he matched with An and Zhisheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ruthless and calculating, adept at ferreting out others' weaknesses, he was of the same stamp as Wan An and Li Zhisheng.

sentences.zh: 嘗嗾蕭彥莊攻李秉，又逐尹旻、羅璟，人皆惡而畏之。

translations.literal: He once incited Xiao Yanzhuang to attack Li Bing, and again expelled Yin Min and Luo Jing; all hated him yet feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He had once set Xiao Yanzhuang on Li Bing, and later drove out Yin Min and Luo Jing; everyone loathed him but dared not defy him.

sentences.zh: 逾年，得風疾去。

translations.literal: After more than a year he took a wind illness and left office.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he resigned, stricken with paralysis.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嗣位，安草登極詔書，禁言官假風聞挾私，中外嘩然。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong succeeded to the throne, An drafted the accession edict forbidding censors to use hearsay for private ends; within and without the court there was uproar.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaozong's accession Wan An drafted the enthronement edict forbidding censors to lodge charges on hearsay for private ends, provoking outrage throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 御史湯鼐詣閣。

translations.literal: Censor Tang Xi went to the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Tang Xi came to the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 安從容言曰：「此裏面意也。

translations.literal: An said calmly: "This is the inner meaning."
translations.idiomatic: Wan An said calmly, "That came from inside the palace."

sentences.zh: 」鼐即以其語奏聞，謂安抑塞言路，歸過於君，無人臣禮。

translations.literal: Xi immediately memorialized his words, saying An blocked the path of remonstrance, shifted blame onto the ruler, and lacked a minister's rites.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Xi at once reported his words to the throne, charging that Wan An had choked off remonstrance, blamed the emperor for his own doing, and violated the duties of a subject.

sentences.zh: 於是庶吉士鄒智，御史文貴、姜洪等交章列其罪狀。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hanlin probationer Zou Zhi, and censors Wen Gui and Jiang Hong, among others, submitted memorials in succession listing his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin probationer Zou Zhi and censors Wen Gui, Jiang Hong, and others then submitted memorial after memorial detailing his offenses.

sentences.zh: 先是，歙人倪進賢者，粗知書，無行，諂事安，日與講房中術。

translations.literal: Earlier, one Ni Jinxian of She, who roughly knew books and had no conduct, flattered and served An and daily discussed bedroom arts with him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier there had been one Ni Jinxian of She, barely literate and utterly without principle, who fawned on Wan An and daily discussed sexual cultivation techniques with him.

sentences.zh: 安昵之，因令就試，得進士。

translations.literal: An was fond of him and therefore had him take the examination; he obtained the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: Wan An favored him and had him sit for the examinations; he passed as a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 授為庶吉士，除御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed a probationer and then made a censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a Hanlin probationer and then appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 帝一日於宮中得疏一小篋，則皆論房中術者，末署曰「臣安進」。

translations.literal: One day the emperor in the palace obtained a small casket of memorials—all discussed bedroom arts; at the end it was signed "Your subject An presents."
translations.idiomatic: One day in the palace the emperor found a small box of memorials, all on sexual cultivation techniques, signed at the end "Presented by your subject An."

sentences.zh: 帝命太監懷恩持至閣曰：「此大臣所為耶？

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the eunuch Huai En to carry them to the Grand Secretariat and say: "Is this what a great minister did?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the eunuch Huai En to bring them to the Grand Secretariat and ask, "Would a great minister do this?"

sentences.zh: 」安愧汗伏地，不能出聲。

translations.literal: An, ashamed and sweating, lay prostrate on the ground and could not utter a sound.
translations.idiomatic: Wan An, flushed with shame, prostrated himself and could not speak.

sentences.zh: 及諸臣彈章入，復令恩就安讀之。

translations.literal: When the various ministers' impeachment memorials arrived, the emperor again ordered En to go to An and read them aloud.
translations.idiomatic: When the ministers' impeachment memorials arrived, the emperor again sent Huai En to read them aloud to Wan An.

sentences.zh: 安數跪起求哀，無去意。

translations.literal: An repeatedly knelt and rose to beg for mercy, with no intention of leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Wan An knelt and rose again and again pleading for mercy, yet showed no sign of departing.

sentences.zh: 恩直前摘其牙牌曰：「可出矣。

translations.literal: En went straight forward, plucked his ivory tally, and said: "You may go."
translations.idiomatic: Huai En stepped forward, snatched his ivory tally of office, and said, "You may leave now."

sentences.zh: 」始惶遽索馬歸第，乞休去。

translations.literal: Only then, alarmed and hurried, did he seek a horse, return to his residence, and beg to retire and leave.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Wan An, in panic, send for a horse, hurry home, and submit a request to retire.

sentences.zh: 時年已七十余。

translations.literal: At the time he was already more than seventy years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He was then more than seventy years old.

sentences.zh: 尚於道上望三臺星，冀復用。

translations.literal: Still on the road he gazed at the Three Terraces stars, hoping to be employed again.
translations.idiomatic: Even on the road home he looked up at the Three Terraces stars, hoping for recall to office.

sentences.zh: 居一年卒，贈太師，謚文康。

translations.literal: After one year he died; he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous name Wenkang.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he died and was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor with the posthumous name Wenkang.

sentences.zh: 初，孝穆皇太后之薨，內庭籍籍指萬貴妃。

translations.literal: Initially, at the death of Empress Dowager Xiaomu, the inner court buzzingly pointed at the imperial consort Lady Wan.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Xiaomu died, palace rumor had long fingered the Noble Consort Wan.

sentences.zh: 孝宗立，魚臺縣丞徐項上書發其事。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong took the throne, Xu Xiang, assistant magistrate of Yutai County, memorialized and exposed the matter.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiaozong's accession, Xu Xiang, assistant magistrate of Yutai, memorialized to expose what had happened.

sentences.zh: 廷臣議逮鞫萬氏戚屬曾出入宮掖者。

translations.literal: Court ministers discussed arresting and examining Wan clan relatives who had once entered the palace women's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated arresting and interrogating Wan kinsmen who had once had access to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 安驚懼不知所為，曰：「我久不與萬氏往來矣。

translations.literal: An, alarmed and fearful, knew not what to do and said: "I have long ceased association with the Wan clan."
translations.idiomatic: Wan An was terrified and at a loss, saying, "I have had no dealings with the Wan clan for years."

sentences.zh: 」而劉吉先與萬氏姻，亦自危。

translations.literal: But Liu Ji had earlier had marriage ties with the Wan clan and also feared for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji, who had earlier married into the Wan clan, feared for himself as well.

sentences.zh: 其黨尹直尚在閣，共擬旨寢之。

translations.literal: His clique member Yin Zhi was still in the Grand Secretariat; together they drafted a rescript to shelve the matter.
translations.idiomatic: His ally Yin Zhi remained in the Grand Secretariat; together they drafted an edict to bury the case.

sentences.zh: 孝宗仁厚，亦置不問，安、吉得無事。

translations.literal: Xiaozong was benevolent and generous and also set the matter aside without inquiry; An and Ji escaped trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The benevolent Xiaozong let the matter drop, and both Wan An and Liu Ji escaped unscathed.

sentences.zh: 安在政府二十年，每遇試，必令其門生為考官，子孫甥婿多登第者。

translations.literal: An had been in government twenty years; whenever examinations came he always had his disciples serve as examiners, and his sons, grandsons, and sons-in-law many times passed.
translations.idiomatic: During Wan An's twenty years in power, every examination saw his protégés appointed as examiners, and his sons, grandsons, and sons-in-law repeatedly passed.

sentences.zh: 子翼，南京禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Yi was Vice Minister of Rites at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wan Yi served as Vice Minister of Rites at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 孫弘璧，翰林編修。

translations.literal: His grandson Hongbi was a Hanlin compiler.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Wan Hongbi was a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 安死無幾，翼、弘璧相繼死，安竟無後。

translations.literal: Not long after An's death, Yi and Hongbi died in succession, and An ultimately had no posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Wan An's death his son and grandson died in turn, and his line ended altogether.

sentences.zh: 劉珝，字叔溫，壽光人。

translations.literal: Liu Xu, styled Shuwen, was a man of Shouguang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xu, courtesy name Shuwen, was a native of Shouguang.

sentences.zh: 正統十三年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhengtong he passed as a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the thirteenth year of Zhengtong.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He was made a probationer and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Hanlin as a probationer and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 天順中，歷右中允，侍講東宮。

translations.literal: In the Tianshun reign he passed through the post of Right Vice Director and lectured in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshun reign he served as Right Vice Director and lectured in the heir apparent's palace.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，以舊宮僚屢遷太常卿，兼侍讀學士，直經筵日講。

translations.literal: When Xianzong took the throne, as an old member of the palace staff he was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, concurrently Reader-in-waiting, attending the Classics Colloquium for daily lectures.
translations.idiomatic: At Xianzong's accession, as a former palace tutor he rose repeatedly to Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, also serving as Reader-in-waiting and lecturing daily at the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 成化十年進吏部左侍郎，充講官如故。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chenghua he was advanced to Left Vice Minister of Personnel, continuing as lecturer as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 10 he was promoted to Left Vice Minister of Personnel while continuing his duties as lecturer.

sentences.zh: 珝每進講，反覆開導，詞氣侃侃，聞者為悚。

translations.literal: Whenever Xu entered to lecture he repeatedly opened and guided; his words and tone were earnest, and hearers were struck with awe.
translations.idiomatic: Each time Liu Xu lectured he expounded point by point with unwavering earnestness, and his listeners were moved to awe.

sentences.zh: 學士劉定之稱為講官第一，憲宗亦愛重之。

translations.literal: Academician Liu Dingzhi called him first among lecturers, and Xianzong also loved and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Liu Dingzhi ranked him the finest lecturer of his day, and Xianzong held him in special regard.

sentences.zh: 明年詔以本官兼翰林學士，入閣預機務。

translations.literal: The next year an edict made him, in his present office, also Hanlin academician; he entered the Grand Secretariat to participate in secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year an edict named him Hanlin academician while retaining his present rank, and he entered the Grand Secretariat to share in state secrets.

sentences.zh: 帝每呼「東劉先生」，賜印章一，文曰「嘉猷贊翊」。

translations.literal: The emperor always called him "Eastern Lord Liu," and granted one seal whose inscription read "Fine plans assist and support."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor habitually addressed him as "Eastern Lord Liu" and bestowed a seal inscribed "Fine plans assist and support."

sentences.zh: 尋進吏部尚書，再加太子少保、文淵閣大學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Minister of Personnel, and again made Junior Guardian and Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Minister of Personnel and further honored as Junior Guardian and Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 《文華大訓》成。

translations.literal: The Great Compendium of Literary Cultivation was completed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Great Compendium of Literary Cultivation was completed, he was further honored.

sentences.zh: 加太子太保，進謹身殿大學士。

translations.literal: He was made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and advanced to Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and promoted to Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall.

sentences.zh: 珝性疏直。

translations.literal: Xu by nature was loose and straight.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xu was by nature blunt and forthright.

sentences.zh: 自以宮僚舊臣，遇事無所回護。

translations.literal: Regarding himself as old palace staff, on affairs he nowhere held back.
translations.idiomatic: As a veteran of the heir apparent's household, he never shrank from any matter.

sentences.zh: 員外郎林俊以劾梁芳、繼曉下獄，珝於帝前解之。

translations.literal: Section Vice Director Lin Jun, for impeaching Liang Fang and Ji Xiao, was imprisoned; Xu before the emperor exonerated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Section Vice Director Lin Jun was imprisoned for impeaching Liang Fang and Ji Xiao, Liu Xu pleaded his case before the emperor and secured his release.

sentences.zh: 李孜省輩左道亂政，欲動搖東宮。

translations.literal: Li Zhisheng's sort, by heterodox ways, disrupted government and wished to shake the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhisheng and his ilk practiced heterodox arts, threw government into disorder, and sought to undermine the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 珝密疏諫，謀少阻。

translations.literal: Xu secretly memorialized in remonstrance, and the plot was somewhat blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xu submitted a secret memorial of remonstrance, and their designs were partly thwarted.

sentences.zh: 素薄萬安，嘗斥安負國無恥。

translations.literal: He had always despised Wan An and once denounced An as betraying the state without shame.
translations.idiomatic: He had long held Wan An in contempt and once denounced him as a shameless traitor to the realm.

sentences.zh: 安積忿，日夜思中珝。

translations.literal: An accumulated resentment and day and night thought to strike Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Wan An nursed a grudge and plotted day and night to bring Liu Xu down.

sentences.zh: 初，商輅之劾汪直也，珝與萬安、劉吉助之爭，得罷西廠。

translations.literal: Initially, when Shang Lu impeached Wang Zhi, Xu together with Wan An and Liu Ji helped in the struggle, and the Western Depot was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Shang Lu first moved against Wang Zhi, Liu Xu had joined Wan An and Liu Ji in the fight, and the Western Depot was abolished.

sentences.zh: 他日，珝又折王越於朝，越慚而退。

translations.literal: On another day Xu again rebuked Wang Yue at court, and Yue withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion Liu Xu publicly rebuked Wang Yue at court until Wang Yue withdrew in humiliation.

sentences.zh: 已而西廠復設，珝不能有所諍。

translations.literal: Soon after the Western Depot was re-established, and Xu could not remonstrate effectively.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Western Depot was restored, and Liu Xu proved unable to protest it effectively.

sentences.zh: 至十八年，安見直寵衰，揣知西廠當罷，邀珝同奏。

translations.literal: By the eighteenth year An saw Zhi's favor waning, inferred that the Western Depot should be abolished, and invited Xu to memorialize together.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Wan An saw Wang Zhi's star fading, guessed the Western Depot would be shut down, and asked Liu Xu to join him in memorializing.

sentences.zh: 珝辭不與，安遂獨奏。

translations.literal: Xu declined and would not join; An thereupon memorialized alone.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xu refused; Wan An submitted the memorial alone.

sentences.zh: 疏上，帝頗訝無珝名。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor was quite surprised that Xu's name was not on it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, the emperor was surprised to find Liu Xu's name absent.

sentences.zh: 安陰使人訐珝與直有連。

translations.literal: An secretly sent men to accuse Xu of ties with Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wan An secretly spread word that Liu Xu was connected with Wang Zhi.

sentences.zh: 會珝子鎡邀妓狎飲，裏人趙賓戲為《劉公子曲》，或增飾穢語，雜教坊院本奏之。

translations.literal: It happened that Xu's son Zi invited prostitutes for intimate drinking; the neighbor Zhao Bin playfully composed 《The Lord Liu's Son Ballad》, some added filthy words, and it was performed mixed with brothel play scripts.
translations.idiomatic: About then Liu Xu's son Zi entertained prostitutes; a neighbor, Zhao Bin, wrote a lampoon called 《The Lord Liu's Son Ballad》, to which others added obscene verses that were performed alongside brothel skits.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，決意去珝。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angry and resolved to remove Xu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and resolved to dismiss Liu Xu.

sentences.zh: 遣中官覃昌召安、吉赴西角門，出帝手封書一函示之。

translations.literal: He sent the palace eunuch Tan Chang to summon An and Ji to the West Corner Gate and produced one bundle of the emperor's hand-sealed documents to show them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the eunuch Tan Chang to summon Wan An and Liu Ji to the West Corner Gate and showed them a packet sealed in the emperor's own hand.

sentences.zh: 安等佯驚救。

translations.literal: An and the others feigned alarm to rescue the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Wan An and the others pretended shock and made a show of intervening on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 次日，珝具疏乞休。

translations.literal: The next day Xu fully memorialized, begging to retire.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Liu Xu submitted a formal request to retire.

sentences.zh: 令馳驛，賜月廩、歲隸、白金、楮幣甚厚。

translations.literal: He was ordered a relay horse; monthly grain, yearly stipend, white silver, and paper money were granted very generously.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent home by courier post with lavish gifts of monthly grain, annual stipend, silver, and paper money.

sentences.zh: 其實排珝使去者，安、吉兩人謀也。

translations.literal: In truth those who expelled Xu and made him leave were the plot of An and Ji, the two men.
translations.idiomatic: In truth it was Wan An and Liu Ji who had engineered his removal.

sentences.zh: 時內閣三人，安貪狡，吉陰刻。

translations.literal: At the time there were three in the Grand Secretariat: An was greedy and cunning, Ji secretly harsh.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Secretariat then held three men: Wan An was greedy and treacherous, Liu Ji secretly cruel.

sentences.zh: 珝稍優，顧喜譚論，人目為狂躁。

translations.literal: Xu was somewhat better, only he liked expansive talk; people regarded him as frantic.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xu was somewhat better, but he loved to talk at length and was thought rash and excitable.

sentences.zh: 珝既倉卒引退，而彭華、尹直相繼入內閣，安、吉之黨乃益固。

translations.literal: Since Xu had hastily withdrawn, Peng Hua and Yin Zhi successively entered the Grand Secretariat, and An and Ji's faction then grew more solid.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liu Xu had been hurried from office, Peng Hua and Yin Zhi entered the Grand Secretariat in turn, and the Wan–Liu faction tightened its grip.

sentences.zh: 珝初遭母憂，廬墓三年。

translations.literal: When Xu at first encountered his mother's mourning, he hutted at the grave for three years.
translations.idiomatic: At his mother's death Liu Xu first mourned at her grave in a hut for three years.

sentences.zh: 比歸，侍父盡孝。

translations.literal: When he returned he served his father with full filiality.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home he attended his father with complete filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 父歿，復廬於墓。

translations.literal: When his father died he again hutted at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he again kept vigil at the tomb.

sentences.zh: 弘治三年卒，謚文和。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongzhi he died and was given the posthumous name Wenhe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Hongzhi 3 and was posthumously named Wenhe.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，以言官請，賜祠額曰「昭賢」，仍遣官祭之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing, on the censors' request, a shrine plaque was granted reading "Manifest Worthy," and officials were still sent to sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiajing, at censors' request, his shrine received the plaque title "Manifest Worthy," and the court continued to send officers to offer sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 子鈗，字汝中。

translations.literal: His son Jun, styled Ruzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Jun, courtesy name Ruzhong.

sentences.zh: 八歲時，憲宗召見，愛其聰敏，且拜起如禮，即命為中書舍人。

translations.literal: At age eight, Xianzong summoned him to audience, loved his cleverness, and because his bowing and rising followed ritual, at once appointed him Central Draftsman.
translations.idiomatic: When he was eight, Xianzong received him in audience, delighted in his quick wit, and because he bowed and rose with proper ceremony, immediately appointed him Central Draftsman.

sentences.zh: 宮殿門閾高，同官楊一清常提之出入。

translations.literal: The palace gates' thresholds were high; his colleague Yang Yiqing often lifted him to go in and out.
translations.idiomatic: The palace gate sills were so high that his colleague Yang Yiqing often had to lift him over them when he went in and out.

sentences.zh: 帝慮牙牌易損，命易以銀。

translations.literal: The emperor worried the ivory tally would be easily damaged and ordered it replaced with silver.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feared his ivory tally would wear out easily and ordered it remade in silver.

sentences.zh: 歷官五十余年，嘉靖中至太常卿，兼五經博士，仍供事內閣誥敕房。

translations.literal: He held office more than fifty years; in Jiajing he reached Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, concurrently Five Classics doctorate, and still served in the Grand Secretariat Edict and Patent Office.
translations.idiomatic: He served in office for more than fifty years; under Jiajing he rose to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, concurrently held the Five Classics doctorate, and still worked in the Grand Secretariat's Edict and Patent Office.

sentences.zh: 博學有行誼，與長洲劉棨並淹貫故實，時稱「二劉」。

translations.literal: Learned and with moral conduct, he and Liu Qi of Changzhou alike were steeped in historical facts; the age called them "the Two Liu."
translations.idiomatic: Learned and principled, he and Liu Qi of Changzhou were alike steeped in historical precedent; contemporaries called them "the Two Liu."

sentences.zh: 劉吉，字祐之，博野人。

translations.literal: Liu Ji, styled Youzhi, was a man of Boye.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji, courtesy name Youzhi, was a native of Boye.

sentences.zh: 正統十三年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhengtong he became a metropolitan graduate.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 13 he passed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授編修，充經筵官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin bachelor, appointed compiler, and filled a Classics Lecture post.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a Hanlin bachelor, appointed compiler, and served on the Classics Lecture.

sentences.zh: 《寰宇通志》成，進修撰。

translations.literal: When the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Realm was completed, he was promoted to senior compiler.
translations.idiomatic: When the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Realm was completed, he was promoted to senior compiler.

sentences.zh: 天順四年侍講讀於東宮，以憂歸。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianshun he lectured and read at the Eastern Palace, then returned home on mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun 4 he lectured and read at the Eastern Palace, then went home to mourn.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位。

translations.literal: Xianzong took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong ascended the throne,

sentences.zh: 召纂《英宗實錄》。

translations.literal: He was summoned to compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Yingzong.
translations.idiomatic: he was summoned to compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Yingzong.

sentences.zh: 至京，上疏乞終制。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the capital he memorialized begging to complete mourning.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the capital he memorialized asking to complete his mourning period.

sentences.zh: 不允，進侍讀。

translations.literal: It was not granted; he was advanced to reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied, and he was promoted to reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 《實錄》成，遷侍讀學士，直經筵。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records were completed he was transferred to lecturing academician and attended the Classics Lecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records were finished he was made lecturing academician with regular duty at the Classics Lecture.

sentences.zh: 累遷禮部左侍郎。

translations.literal: He was progressively promoted to Left Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to Left Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 成化十一年與劉珝同受命，兼翰林學士，入閣預機務。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Chenghua he received appointment together with Liu Xu, concurrently Hanlin academician, entering the Grand Secretariat to take part in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 11 he received appointment together with Liu Xu, concurrently as Hanlin academician, and entered the Grand Secretariat to share in state deliberations.

sentences.zh: 尋進禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was promoted to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 孝宗出閤，加太子少保兼文淵閣大學士。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong left the inner quarters, Ji was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong left the palace school, Liu Ji was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 十八年遭父喪，詔起復。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he encountered his father's mourning; an edict ordered recall from mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year his father died; an edict ordered him recalled from mourning.

sentences.zh: 吉三疏懇辭，而陰屬貴戚萬喜為之地，得不允。

translations.literal: Ji thrice memorialized earnestly to decline, yet secretly had the powerful kinsman Wan Xi press his case, and it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji thrice memorialized earnestly to decline, yet secretly had the powerful kinsman Wan Xi lobby on his behalf, and the court would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 《文華大訓》成，加太子太保，進武英殿大學士。

translations.literal: When the Great Compendium of Literary Cultivation was completed, he was made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the Great Compendium of Literary Cultivation was completed, he was made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall.

sentences.zh: 久之，進戶部尚書、謹身殿大學士，尋加少保兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: After a long time he was promoted to Minister of Revenue and Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall; soon he was also made Junior Mentor and concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was promoted to Minister of Revenue and Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall, and soon after was made Junior Mentor while also serving as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 初，吉與萬安、劉珝在成化時，帝失德，無所規正，時有「紙糊三閣老，泥塑六尚書」之謠。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ji together with Wan An and Liu Xu in the Chenghua reign, when the emperor's conduct failed, offered no correction—hence the rhyme "three Grand Secretaries of pasted paper, six ministers of molded clay."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Chenghua reign, Liu Ji together with Wan An and Liu Xu had done nothing to correct the emperor's misconduct, and people had a rhyme: "three Grand Secretaries of pasted paper, six ministers of molded clay."

sentences.zh: 至是見孝宗仁明，同列徐溥、劉健皆正人，而吉於閣臣居首，兩人有論建，吉亦暑名，復時時為正論，竊美名以自蓋。

translations.literal: Now seeing Xiaozong benevolent and clear, and colleagues Xu Pu and Liu Jian both upright men, while Ji as senior among secretaries—when the two offered policy proposals Ji also signed his name, and from time to time voiced upright opinion, stealing a good name to cover himself.
translations.idiomatic: Now he saw Xiaozong as benevolent and clear-sighted, and his colleagues Xu Pu and Liu Jian were both upright men; as the senior Grand Secretary, whenever the two offered policy critiques Liu Ji also signed his name, and from time to time voiced upright opinions, stealing a good reputation to cover himself.

sentences.zh: 弘治二年二月旱，帝令儒臣撰文禱雨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongzhi, second month, drought; the emperor ordered Confucian officials to compose texts praying for rain.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 2, during a drought in the second month, the emperor ordered Confucian officials to compose texts praying for rain.

sentences.zh: 吉等言：「邇者奸徒襲李孜省、鄧常恩故術，見月宿在畢，天將陰雨，遂奏請祈禱，覬一驗以希進用。

translations.literal: Ji and others said: "Of late villains have revived the old arts of Li Zisheng and Deng Chang'en; seeing the moon's lodge in Bi, they claim heaven will soon send cloudy rain, and so memorialize begging prayer, hoping one fulfillment will win advancement."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji and the others said: "Of late villains have revived the old arts of Li Zisheng and Deng Chang'en; seeing the moon's lodge in Bi, they claim that heaven will soon send rain, and so they memorialize begging for prayer, hoping that one fulfilled omen will win them advancement."

sentences.zh: 倖門一開，爭言祈禱，要寵召禍，實基於此。

translations.literal: "Once the gate of favor opens, all vie to speak of prayer; courting favor invites disaster—the root lies here."
translations.idiomatic: "Once the gate of favoritism opens, everyone will vie to speak of prayer; courting favor invites disaster—and the root of it lies here."

sentences.zh: 祝文不敢奉詔。

translations.literal: "We dare not accept the edict to draft the prayer text."
translations.idiomatic: "We dare not accept the edict to draft the prayer text."

sentences.zh: 」帝意悟，遂已之。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was enlightened and he stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took their point and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 五月以災異請帝修德防微，慎終如始。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on account of abnormal omens, they asked the emperor to cultivate virtue and guard against the slightest lapse, treating the end as earnestly as the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, citing abnormal omens, they urged the emperor to cultivate virtue, guard against the slightest lapse, and treat the end as earnestly as the beginning.

sentences.zh: 八月又以災異陳七事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month they again set forth seven matters on account of abnormal omens.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month they again set forth seven matters in light of abnormal omens.

sentences.zh: 代王獻海青，吉等言登極詔書已卻四方貢獻，乞勿受。

translations.literal: The Prince of Dai presented a sea hawk; Ji and others said the accession edict had already declined tribute from all quarters and begged that it not be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Dai presented a sea hawk; Liu Ji and the others said the accession edict had already declined tribute from all quarters and begged that it not be accepted.

sentences.zh: 明年三月偕同列上言：「陛下聖質清羸，與先帝不同。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year they joined colleagues in memorializing: "Your Majesty's sacred constitution is clear and slight, unlike the Former Emperor's."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the following year they joined their colleagues in memorializing: "Your Majesty's sacred constitution is clear and slight, unlike the Former Emperor's."

sentences.zh: 凡宴樂遊觀，一切嗜好之事，宜悉減省。

translations.literal: "Every feast, amusement, tour, and indulgence should be wholly reduced."
translations.idiomatic: "Every feast, amusement, excursion, and indulgence should be wholly reduced."

sentences.zh: 左右近臣有請如先帝故事者，當以太祖、太宗典故斥退之。

translations.literal: "If close attendants should ask to follow the Former Emperor's precedents, they should be rebuffed with the models of Taizu and Taizong."
translations.idiomatic: "If close attendants ask to follow the Former Emperor's precedents, they should be rebuffed with the models of Taizu and Taizong."

sentences.zh: 祖宗令節宴遊皆有時，陛下法祖宗可也。

translations.literal: "Our ancestors set times for festival feasts and excursions; Your Majesty may take the ancestors as law."
translations.idiomatic: "Our ancestors set fixed times for festival feasts and excursions; Your Majesty may take the ancestors as your law."

sentences.zh: 」土魯番使者貢獅子還，帝令內閣草敕，遣中官送之。

translations.literal: The Turfan envoy who had presented a lion was returning; the emperor ordered the Grand Secretariat to draft an edict and sent an inner eunuch to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: The Turfan envoy who had presented a lion was returning; the emperor ordered the Grand Secretariat to draft an edict and sent an inner eunuch to escort him home.

sentences.zh: 吉等言不宜優寵太過，使番戎輕中國。

translations.literal: Ji and others said he should not be favored beyond measure lest frontier peoples hold China cheap.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji and the others said he should not be favored beyond measure, lest the frontier peoples hold China cheap.

sentences.zh: 事遂寢。

translations.literal: The affair was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The affair was dropped.

sentences.zh: 既又言：「獅子諸獸，日飼二羊，歲當用七百二十，又守視校尉日五十人，皆繁費。

translations.literal: They spoke again: "Lions and other beasts are fed two sheep daily—seven hundred twenty a year—and fifty guards watch them each day; all is wasteful extravagance."
translations.idiomatic: They spoke again: "Lions and other beasts are fed two sheep a day—seven hundred twenty a year—and fifty guards watch over them daily; all of this is wasteful extravagance."

sentences.zh: 宜絕諸獸食，聽自斃。

translations.literal: "Cut off food for all such beasts and let them die of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: "Cut off food for all such beasts and let them die on their own."

sentences.zh: 」帝不能用。

translations.literal: The emperor could not adopt this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not accept this.

sentences.zh: 十二月，星變，又言：「邇者妖星出天津，歷杵臼，迫營室，其占為兵，為饑，為水旱。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, with a change of stars, they again said: "Of late an evil star appeared at Tianjin, passed Pestle and Mortar, and pressed Camp; its portent is war, famine, and flood or drought."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, with a stellar anomaly, they again said: "Of late an evil star appeared at Tianjin, passed Pestle and Mortar, and pressed Camp; its portent is war, famine, and flood or drought."

sentences.zh: 今兩畿、河南、山西、陜西旱蝗；

translations.literal: "Now the two capitals regions, Henan, Shanxi, and Shaanxi suffer drought and locusts;"
translations.idiomatic: "Now the two metropolitan regions, Henan, Shanxi, and Shaanxi suffer drought and locusts;"

sentences.zh: 四川、湖廣歲不登。

translations.literal: "Sichuan and Huguang have lean harvests."
translations.idiomatic: "Sichuan and Huguang have had poor harvests."

sentences.zh: 倘明年復然，恐盜賊竊發，禍亂將作。

translations.literal: "If next year is the same, I fear thieves may rise in secret and calamity and rebellion will follow."
translations.idiomatic: "If next year is the same, I fear bandits may rise in secret and calamity and rebellion will follow."

sentences.zh: 願陛下節用度，罷宴遊，屏讒言，斥異教，留懷經史，講求治道。

translations.literal: "We pray Your Majesty will economize expenditure, cease feasts and excursions, banish slander, reject heterodox cults, keep the classics in mind, and study the way of governance."
translations.idiomatic: "We pray that Your Majesty will economize expenditure, cease feasts and excursions, banish slander, reject heterodox cults, keep the classics in mind, and study the way of governance."

sentences.zh: 沙河修橋，江西造瓷器，南海子繕垣墻，俱非急務，宜悉停止。

translations.literal: "Repairing the bridge at Sha River, making porcelain in Jiangxi, and mending walls at the Southern Park are none urgent—let all be halted."
translations.idiomatic: "Repairing the bridge on the Sha River, making porcelain in Jiangxi, and mending walls at the Southern Park are none of them urgent—let all be halted."

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and adopted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and adopted their advice.

sentences.zh: 帝惑近習言，頗崇祈禱事，發經牌令閣臣作贊，又令擬神將封號。

translations.literal: The emperor, swayed by close attendants' words, came greatly to esteem prayer; he issued sutra placards ordering Grand Secretaries to compose encomia and also commanded them to draft titles for divine generals.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, swayed by his close attendants, came greatly to esteem prayer; he issued sutra placards ordering the Grand Secretaries to compose encomia and also commanded them to draft titles for divine generals.

sentences.zh: 吉等極言邪說當斥。

translations.literal: Ji and others strenuously argued heterodox doctrines must be rejected.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji and the others strenuously argued that such heterodox doctrines must be rejected.

sentences.zh: 吉自帝初即位進少傅，兼太子太師，吏部尚書。

translations.literal: From the emperor's first accession Ji was advanced to Junior Mentor, concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: From the emperor's first accession Liu Ji had been advanced to Junior Mentor, concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 及《憲宗實錄》成。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianzong were completed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianzong were completed,

sentences.zh: 又進少師、華蓋殿大學士。

translations.literal: He was further made Junior Preceptor and Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall.
translations.idiomatic: he was further made Junior Preceptor and Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall.

sentences.zh: 吉柄政久，權勢烜赫。

translations.literal: Ji held power long; his authority blazed bright.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji had held power for a long time; his authority blazed bright.

sentences.zh: 帝初傾心聽信，後眷頗衰。

translations.literal: At first the emperor leaned on him and trusted him; later his favor waned considerably.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor leaned on him and trusted him; later the emperor's regard waned considerably.

sentences.zh: 而吉終無去誌。

translations.literal: Yet Ji to the end showed no wish to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Liu Ji to the end showed no wish to leave office.

sentences.zh: 五年，帝欲封後弟伯爵，命吉撰誥券。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the emperor wished to enfeoff the empress's younger brother as earl and ordered Ji to draft the patent and certificate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the emperor wished to enfeoff the empress's younger brother as earl and ordered Liu Ji to draft the patent and certificate.

sentences.zh: 吉言必盡封二太后家子弟方可。

translations.literal: Ji said both empress dowagers' clansmen must all be enfeoffed alike before this could be done.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji said that the clansmen of both empress dowagers must all be enfeoffed alike before this could be done.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅，遣中官至其家，諷令致仕，始上章引退。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased; he sent a eunuch to Ji's home to hint that he retire, whereupon Ji at last submitted a withdrawal memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased; he sent a eunuch to Liu Ji's home to hint that he retire, whereupon Liu Ji at last submitted a memorial withdrawing from office.

sentences.zh: 良賜敕，馳驛如故事。

translations.literal: He was graciously granted an edict and post horses under established precedent.
translations.idiomatic: He was graciously granted an edict and post horses under established precedent.

sentences.zh: 吉多智數，善附會，自緣飾，銳於營私，時為言路所攻。

translations.literal: Ji was full of stratagems and skilled at trimming his sails; he adorned himself and was keen to pursue private profit, and from time to time came under attack from the remonstrance officials.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji was full of stratagems and skilled at trimming his sails; he adorned himself and was keen to pursue private profit, and from time to time came under attack from the remonstrance officials.

sentences.zh: 居內閣十八年，人目之為「劉綿花」，以其耐彈也。

translations.literal: Eighteen years in the Grand Secretariat—men called him "Liu Cotton Flower" for how he endured being bounced.
translations.idiomatic: After eighteen years in the Grand Secretariat, people called him "Liu Cotton Flower" for how he endured being bounced about by criticism.

sentences.zh: 吉疑其言出下第舉子，因請舉人三試不第者，不得復會試。

translations.literal: Ji suspected the saying came from failed metropolitan candidates and therefore requested that any juren who failed the metropolitan exam three times should not sit again.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji suspected the saying came from failed metropolitan candidates and therefore requested that any provincial graduate who failed the metropolitan examination three times should not sit again.

sentences.zh: 時適當會試期，舉子已群集都下，禮部為請。

translations.literal: The metropolitan exam happened to fall just then; candidates had already gathered in the capital, and the Ministry of Rites petitioned on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The metropolitan examination happened to fall just then; candidates had already gathered in the capital, and the Ministry of Rites petitioned on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 詔姑許入試，後如令。

translations.literal: An edict allowed them to sit this once; hereafter the rule would apply.
translations.idiomatic: An edict allowed them to sit this once; hereafter the rule would apply.

sentences.zh: 已而吉罷，令亦不行。

translations.literal: Before long Ji left office and the order never took effect.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Liu Ji left office and the order never took effect.

sentences.zh: 吉歸，逾年卒。

translations.literal: Ji returned home and died the following year.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji returned home and died the following year.

sentences.zh: 贈太師，謚文穆。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous name Wenmu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous name Wenmu.

sentences.zh: 尹直，字正言，泰和人。

translations.literal: Yin Zhi, styled Zhengyan, was a man of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhi, courtesy name Zhengyan, was a native of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 景泰五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jingtai he became a metropolitan graduate.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 5 he passed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin bachelor and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a Hanlin bachelor and appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 成化初，充經筵講官，與修《英宗實錄》。

translations.literal: Early in Chenghua he served as lecturer on the Classics Lecture and helped compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Yingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chenghua he served as lecturer on the Classics Lecture and helped compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Yingzong.

sentences.zh: 總裁欲革去景泰帝號，引漢昌邑、更始為比。

translations.literal: The chief editor wished to strip the Jingtai emperor's title, citing the Han cases of King of Changyi and Emperor Gengshi as parallels.
translations.idiomatic: The chief editor wished to strip the Jingtai emperor's title, citing the Han cases of the King of Changyi and Emperor Gengshi as parallels.

sentences.zh: 直辨曰：「《實錄》中有初為大臣，後為軍民者。

translations.literal: Zhi rebutted: "In Veritable Records there are cases who were first great ministers and later soldiers or commoners."
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhi rebutted: "In the Veritable Records there are men who were first great ministers and later soldiers or commoners."

sentences.zh: 方居官時，則稱某官某，既罷去而後改稱。

translations.literal: "While still in office one calls them by title; only after removal does the record change the designation."
translations.idiomatic: "While still in office one calls them by their title; only after they leave office does the record change the designation."

sentences.zh: 如漢府以謀逆降庶人，其未反時，書王書叔如故也。

translations.literal: "As when a Han prince was demoted to commoner for conspiracy—before he rebelled, he is still written as 'king' and as 'uncle' as before."
translations.idiomatic: "As when a Han prince was demoted to commoner for conspiracy—before he rebelled, the record still calls him 'king' and 'uncle' as before."

sentences.zh: 豈有逆計其反，而即降從庶人之號者哉！

translations.literal: "How could one, anticipating rebellion, at once lower him to a commoner's style!"
translations.idiomatic: "How could one, anticipating rebellion, at once demote him to a commoner's style!"

sentences.zh: 且昌邑旋立旋廢，景泰帝則為宗廟社稷主七年。

translations.literal: "Moreover the King of Changyi was enthroned and deposed in quick succession, whereas the Jingtai emperor was lord of the ancestral temples and altars for seven years."
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover the King of Changyi was enthroned and deposed in quick succession, whereas the Jingtai emperor was lord of the ancestral temples and altars for seven years."

sentences.zh: 更始無所受命，景泰帝則策命於母後。

translations.literal: "Gengshi received no mandate; the Jingtai emperor was invested by edict from the empress dowager."
translations.idiomatic: "Gengshi received no mandate; the Jingtai emperor was invested by edict from the empress dowager."

sentences.zh: 當時定傾危難之中，微帝則京師非國家有。

translations.literal: "In the crisis when the state teetered, without him the capital would not have remained the dynasty's."
translations.idiomatic: "In the crisis when the state teetered, without him the capital would not have remained the dynasty's."

sentences.zh: 雖易儲失德，然能不惑於盧忠、徐振之言，卒全兩宮，以至今日。

translations.literal: "Though changing the heir was a fault, he was not misled by Lu Zhong and Xu Zhen, and in the end preserved both palaces down to the present day."
translations.idiomatic: "Though changing the heir was a fault, he was not misled by Lu Zhong and Xu Zhen, and in the end preserved both palaces down to the present day."

sentences.zh: 其功過足相準，不宜去帝號。

translations.literal: "Merit and fault balance; the imperial title should not be removed."
translations.idiomatic: "Merit and fault balance; the imperial title should not be removed."

sentences.zh: 」時不能難。

translations.literal: At the time they could not refute him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time they could not refute him.

sentences.zh: 既成，進侍讀，歷侍讀學士。

translations.literal: When the work was done he was promoted to reader-in-waiting and rose through lecturing academician.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished he was promoted to reader-in-waiting and rose through lecturing academician.

sentences.zh: 六年上疏乞纂修《大明通典》，並續成《宋元綱目》，章下所司。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he memorialized begging to compile the Grand Statutes of the Great Ming and continue completing the Outline of Song and Yuan; the memorial was sent to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he memorialized asking to compile the Grand Statutes of the Great Ming and to continue completing the Outline of Song and Yuan; the memorial was sent to the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 十一年遷禮部右侍郎，辭，不許。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to Right Vice Minister of Rites and declined; permission was refused.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was transferred to Right Vice Minister of Rites and declined; the court would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服除，起南京吏部右侍郎，就改禮部左侍郎。

translations.literal: On his father's mourning, when the mourning period ended he was recalled as Right Vice Minister of Personnel at Nanjing, then immediately shifted to Left Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died and mourning ended, he was recalled as Right Vice Minister of Personnel at Nanjing, then immediately shifted to Left Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二十二年春，召佐兵部。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-second year he was summoned to assist the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-second year he was summoned to assist the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 占城王古來為安南所逼，棄國來求援。

translations.literal: The king of Champa, Gulai, was pressed by Annam, abandoned his state, and came begging aid.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Champa, Gulai, was pressed by Annam, abandoned his kingdom, and came begging for aid.

sentences.zh: 議者欲送之還，直曰：「彼窮來歸，我若驅使還國，是殺之也。

translations.literal: Deliberators wished to send him back; Zhi said: "He comes to us in extremity; if we drive him home, we kill him."
translations.idiomatic: Deliberators wished to send him back; Yin Zhi said: "He comes to us in extremity; if we drive him back to his kingdom, we kill him."

sentences.zh: 宜遣大臣即詢，量宜處置。

translations.literal: "A grand minister should be sent at once to inquire and dispose as fit."
translations.idiomatic: "A senior minister should be sent at once to inquire and dispose of the matter as circumstances require."

sentences.zh: 」詔從之，命都御史屠滽往。

translations.literal: The court approved; Censor-in-chief Tu Yong was ordered to go.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved; Censor-in-chief Tu Yong was ordered to go.

sentences.zh: 貴州鎮巡官奏苗反，請發兵，廷議將從之。

translations.literal: Guizhou circuit defense officials reported Miao rebellion and asked for troops; court discussion was about to consent.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou frontier defense officials reported a Miao rebellion and asked for troops; court deliberation was about to consent.

sentences.zh: 直言起釁邀功，不可信。

translations.literal: Zhi said they were stirring quarrels to invite merit—untrustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhi said they were stirring up trouble to claim merit—untrustworthy.

sentences.zh: 命官往勘，果無警。

translations.literal: Officers were ordered to investigate; in fact there was no alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Officers were sent to investigate; in fact there was no alarm.

sentences.zh: 是年九月改戶部兼翰林學士，入內閣。

translations.literal: That year in the ninth month he was shifted to the Ministry of Revenue with concurrent Hanlin academician and entered the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the ninth month he was shifted to the Ministry of Revenue with concurrent Hanlin academician and entered the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 逾月，進兵部尚書，加太子太保。

translations.literal: A month later he was promoted to Minister of War and made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he was promoted to Minister of War and made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 直明敏博學，練習朝章，而躁於進取。

translations.literal: Zhi was bright, keen, and learned, practiced in court regulations, yet rash in advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhi was bright, keen, and learned, well versed in court regulations, yet rash in his pursuit of advancement.

sentences.zh: 性矜忌，不自檢飭，與吏部尚書尹旻相惡。

translations.literal: By nature proud and jealous, he did not restrain himself and was at odds with Minister of Personnel Yin Min.
translations.idiomatic: By nature proud and jealous, he did not restrain himself and was at odds with Minister of Personnel Yin Min.

sentences.zh: 直初覬禮部侍郎，而旻薦他人。

translations.literal: At first Zhi coveted the vice ministership of rites, but Min recommended another.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhi had first hoped for the vice ministership of rites, but Yin Min recommended someone else.

sentences.zh: 直以中旨得之。

translations.literal: Zhi obtained it by secret edict.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhi received the post by secret edict instead.

sentences.zh: 次日遇旻於朝，舉笏謝。

translations.literal: The next day he met Min at court and raised his tablet in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he met Yin Min at court and raised his tablet in thanks.

sentences.zh: 旻曰：「公所謂簡在帝心者。

translations.literal: Min said: "What you call being singled out in the emperor's heart."
translations.idiomatic: Yin Min said, "So much for being singled out in the emperor's heart."

sentences.zh: 」自是怨益深。

translations.literal: From this their enmity grew deeper.
translations.idiomatic: From then on their enmity only deepened.

sentences.zh: 後在南部八年，郁郁不得誌，屬其黨萬安、彭華謀內召，旻輒持不可。

translations.literal: Later, in the south for eight years, he was depressed and unfulfilled; he had his faction Wan An and Peng Hua plot recall to the capital, and Min always opposed it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, during eight years in the south, he brooded over his thwarted ambitions; he had his allies Wan An and Peng Hua scheme for his recall, and Yin Min consistently blocked it.

sentences.zh: 諸朝臣亦皆畏直，幸其在南。

translations.literal: Court ministers also all feared Zhi and were glad he was in the south.
translations.idiomatic: The court ministers feared Yin Zhi as well and were relieved that he remained in the south.

sentences.zh: 及推兵部左、右侍郎，吏部列何琮等八人。

translations.literal: When left and right vice ministers of war were to be chosen, the Ministry of Personnel listed eight men including He Cong.
translations.idiomatic: When left and right vice ministers of war were to be chosen, the Ministry of Personnel nominated eight candidates including He Cong.

sentences.zh: 詔用琮，而直以安、華及李孜省力，中旨召還。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Cong, but Zhi through the efforts of An, Hua, and Li Zisheng obtained a secret edict recalling him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed He Cong, but through Wan An, Peng Hua, and Li Zisheng, Yin Zhi secured a secret edict recalling him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 至是修怨，與孜省等比。

translations.literal: Now he nursed his grudge and aligned with Zisheng and his like.
translations.idiomatic: Now he settled old scores and joined forces with Li Zisheng and his faction.

sentences.zh: 陷旻父子得罪，又構罷江西巡撫閔珪，物論喧然不平。

translations.literal: He framed Min and his son into guilt, and also engineered the dismissal of Jiangxi grand coordinator Min Gui; public opinion was loudly indignant.
translations.idiomatic: He framed Yin Min and his son, engineered the dismissal of Jiangxi Grand Coordinator Min Gui, and public opinion boiled with outrage.

sentences.zh: 刑部郎袁清者，安私人，又幸於內侍郭閏。

translations.literal: Yuan Qing of the Ministry of Justice was An's private man and also favored by the inner attendant Guo Run.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qing, a director in the Ministry of Justice, was Wan An's protégé and also enjoyed favor with the inner attendant Guo Run.

sentences.zh: 勘事浙江，夌轢諸大吏，吏部尚書李裕惡之。

translations.literal: Investigating affairs in Zhejiang, he bullied senior officials; Minister of Personnel Li Yu detested him.
translations.idiomatic: While investigating affairs in Zhejiang he bullied senior officials, and Minister of Personnel Li Yu detested him.

sentences.zh: 比還，即除紹興知府。

translations.literal: On his return he was at once made prefect of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was immediately appointed prefect of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 清懼，累章求改，裕極論其罪，下詔獄。

translations.literal: Qing was afraid and submitted repeated memorials asking for reassignment; Yu argued his crimes to the utmost and he was sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qing panicked and submitted repeated memorials asking for reassignment; Li Yu denounced his crimes in full and had him sent to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 安、閏以屬直，為言於孜省，取中旨赦之，改知鄖陽。

translations.literal: An and Run entrusted him to Zhi, who spoke to Zisheng; a secret edict pardoned him and he was made prefect of Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wan An and Guo Run appealed to Yin Zhi, who spoke to Li Zisheng; a secret edict pardoned Yuan Qing and appointed him prefect of Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 孝宗立，進士李文祥，御史湯鼐、姜洪、繆樗，庶吉士鄒智等連章劾直。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong acceded, the metropolitan graduate Li Wenxiang and the censors Tang Xi, Jiang Hong, and Miu Chu, and the Hanlin bachelor Zou Zhi and others submitted successive memorials impeaching Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong acceded, metropolitan graduate Li Wenxiang, censors Tang Xi, Jiang Hong, and Miu Chu, Hanlin bachelor Zou Zhi, and others submitted successive memorials impeaching Yin Zhi.

sentences.zh: 給事中宋琮及御史許斌言直自初為侍郎以至入閣，夤緣攀附，皆取中旨。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Song Cong and the censor Xu Bin said that from Zhi's first post as vice minister through entering the Grand Secretariat, he had curried favor and climbed by secret edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Song Cong and censor Xu Bin charged that from his first vice ministership through entering the Grand Secretariat, Yin Zhi had curried favor and secured every promotion by secret edict.

sentences.zh: 帝於是薄其為人，令致仕。

translations.literal: The emperor then thought lightly of his character and ordered him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then lost regard for him and ordered him to retire.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年表賀萬壽，並以太子年當出閤，上《承華箴》，引先朝少保黃淮事，冀召對。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Hongzhi he presented a congratulatory memorial for the imperial birthday and, because the heir apparent's age called for leaving the palace school, submitted Admonitions for the Eastern Palace, citing the former Junior Guardian Huang Huai, hoping for a court audience.
translations.idiomatic: In 1496 he presented birthday congratulations and, noting that the heir apparent had reached the age to leave the palace school, submitted Admonitions for the Eastern Palace, citing the former Junior Guardian Huang Huai in hope of a court audience.

sentences.zh: 帝卻之。

translations.literal: The emperor declined it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor declined.

sentences.zh: 正德中卒，謚文和。

translations.literal: He died in the Zhengde period and was given the posthumous title Wenhe.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Zhengde reign and was given the posthumous title Wenhe.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：《易》稱內君子外小人，為泰；

translations.literal: The appraiser says: The Changes states that inner gentleman and outer petty man make peace;
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: The Book of Changes says that when gentlemen are within and petty men without, there is peace;

sentences.zh: 外君子內小人，為否。

translations.literal: outer gentleman and inner petty man make obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: when gentlemen are without and petty men within, there is obstruction.

sentences.zh: 況端揆之寄，百僚具瞻者乎！

translations.literal: How much more when the charge is the chief helm, upon whom all officials look!
translations.idiomatic: How much more when the charge is the chief helm of state, upon whom all officials look!

sentences.zh: 陳循以下諸人，雖不為大奸慝，而居心刻忮，務逞己私。

translations.literal: Chen Xun and the men below him, though not great villains, were by intent harsh and jealous and bent on gratifying private ends.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun and those who followed, though not great villains, were harsh and jealous at heart and bent on gratifying private ends.

sentences.zh: 同己者比，異己者忌；

translations.literal: Those like themselves they grouped with; those unlike they resented;
translations.idiomatic: They banded with those who agreed with them and resented those who did not;

sentences.zh: 比則相援，忌則相軋。

translations.literal: grouping they aided one another, resenting they crushed one another.
translations.idiomatic: in alliance they supported one another, in resentment they crushed one another.

sentences.zh: 至萬安、劉吉要結近幸，蒙恥固位。

translations.literal: As for Wan An and Liu Ji, they courted those near the throne, endured shame, and clung to office.
translations.idiomatic: As for Wan An and Liu Ji, they courted those near the throne, endured shame, and clung to power.

sentences.zh: 猶幸同列多賢，相與彌縫匡救，而穢跡昭彰，小人之歸，何可掩哉！

translations.literal: Yet fortunately many colleagues were worthy and together patched and remedied matters; still their foul tracks were plain—such is the lot of petty men; how can it be concealed!
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately many of their colleagues were worthy men who together patched and remedied matters; yet their foul conduct was plain for all to see—the lot of petty men cannot be concealed.
